# Platform research and executable plan

Researched 14 October 2026. Recommendations below are project-specific engineering judgments grounded in the linked official sources; they are not vendor promises or implemented features. Omar's framework proficiency, laptops, weekly hours, university calendar and paid budget remain unverified. The proposal's 1,500 EGP is historical total project budget, not evidence that recurring cloud/GPU spending is affordable.

## Decision register

### P-D01 — Start the platform now, with one working vertical slice
Recommendation: Omar owns contracts, persistence, authorization and a minimal asset→evidence→assessment screen immediately. Allocate provisionally 75% platform foundation/integration and 25% helping Hams expose and consume AI contracts during the first fortnight; adjust after the skills spike. This is a planning estimate, not a researched universal ratio. Do not wait for a finished classifier or complete scanner: fixture payloads implement the same versioned contracts as real adapters. A mocked UI alone does not prove integration; by the first discussion one real asset observation must cross API→database→assessment→UI. Why Omar: user-confirmed platform experience; not a claim he already knows FastAPI or React. Hams owns experiments, Omar owns production integration. Reviewers are Mahrous for authorization/assessment, Amr for collectors and Shams for source provenance.

### P-D02 — Modular Python backend, separate workers and privileged runner
Recommend FastAPI as a conditional default: OpenAPI/JSON Schema and Python type-based validation fit the AI/data integration boundary [SRC-P01]. Compare Django: built-in accounts, groups, permissions, cookie sessions and admin reduce authentication/admin implementation, but object permissions and login throttling still need deliberate work [SRC-P02]. Django + a documented API layer is the strongest fallback if Omar is materially more effective with it. NestJS supplies structured TypeScript modules/guards and suits a strong TS team [SRC-P03]; here it adds a Python service boundary for ML and most collectors. Do not claim FastAPI is automatically more secure or faster for this workload. Gate: Omar implements one validated asset endpoint, migration, authentication seam and test in at most two focused working days. If framework learning dominates, use the proven team option and retain the contracts.

One codebase with modules inventory, intelligence, assessment, campaigns, identity, AI gateway and integration is a recommendation to control five-person coordination cost. Workers may be separate processes using the same domain package; this is not an initial microservices program. Split privileged scan/patch execution from the internet-facing API and LLM regardless. Microservices become justified by measured independent scaling or a required trust/deployment boundary, not by drawing more boxes. Neither API nor assistant receives arbitrary shell execution. [SRC-P01,SRC-P19,SRC-P22,SRC-P23]

### P-D03 — React + TypeScript + Vite for the authenticated dashboard
React's own documentation permits a build-tool route but highlights that routing/data-fetching choices remain your responsibility [SRC-P04]. Vite supports the build pipeline [SRC-P05]. Recommend this bounded SPA because the main experience is private dashboards and job progress with an existing Python API; same-origin deployment reduces cross-origin configuration. Next.js can render statically or on a server [SRC-P06], and is preferable if public SEO content/server rendering becomes central or Omar already knows it well. Its server capabilities are extra operating surface if unused; static-export features have limitations. Do not call Next.js inherently insecure. Gate: keyboard-accessible asset table, detail route and pending/error/empty states using the real API contract. Choose maintained router/data-fetching packages only after a small current dependency review; do not freeze a library list from familiarity alone.

### P-D04 — PostgreSQL relational core + JSONB evidence; conditional pgvector
Normalize entities and foreign keys; retain vendor/raw records separately with source/revision/hash. JSONB supports flexible indexed fields but is not a reason to put the entire product in one JSON column [SRC-P07]. MySQL has a capable native JSON type [SRC-P08]; reject the false claim it cannot store this data. PostgreSQL is recommended because the relational asset/advisory/finding workflow, row policies and optional pgvector can live in one database. MySQL is a valid alternative if team operations are much stronger there, with retrieval isolated behind an adapter.

pgvector provides exact and approximate search alongside ordinary SQL [SRC-P09]. Begin retrieval evaluation with exact identifiers, metadata filters and lexical search; add embeddings only when Hams shows benefit. Approximate indexes can reduce recall, and filters interact with ANN retrieval; measure recall after authorization/vendor/version filters. Qdrant is a specialized vector alternative with filtering and a separate service [SRC-P10]; choose it only after measured corpus/index/concurrency requirements exceed the simpler design. It adds synchronization, backups and security configuration. RAG remains a derived index, not the authoritative CVE/applicability database. Keep embedding model/version/dimension in records; reindex on model changes.

Use SQLAlchemy transaction-scoped sessions and Alembic reviewed migrations if FastAPI is selected [SRC-P25,SRC-P26]. Django ORM/migrations would replace these if Django wins; do not run both ORMs without a specific need. A schema change needs upgrade verification and a recovery plan; down migrations cannot recreate deleted data. App roles must not connect as superuser or table owner if relying on PostgreSQL row policies [SRC-P11]. First version can be single-organization with explicit scope checks; do not market it as tenant-isolated SaaS until cross-tenant tests pass.

### P-D05 — Durable job ledger/outbox + Celery broker; benchmark RabbitMQ first
FastAPI background tasks execute in-process and its docs suggest larger tools for heavy work [SRC-P12]. They are unsuitable as the sole durability mechanism for scan, ingest or patch workflows. Recommend a PostgreSQL job/attempt ledger and transactional outbox as business truth. Celery + RabbitMQ is the first broker candidate; Celery supports RabbitMQ and Redis as stable transports, with SQL databases available for durable result storage [SRC-P13]. Use small messages containing job IDs, not asset credentials or full evidence.

RabbitMQ acknowledgements and publisher confirms address different delivery legs; they do not create exactly-once side effects [SRC-P14]. Celery retry/late acknowledgement also requires idempotent design [SRC-P15]. Redis is simpler if already needed but Celery documents visibility timeout redelivery and scheduling caveats [SRC-P16]; Redis 8+ license choices are AGPLv3/RSALv2/SSPLv1, not a blanket BSD claim [SRC-P17]. RQ is attractive for simpler Python jobs [SRC-P18], but application approval/attempt/evidence logic is still required. A PostgreSQL-only queue avoids a broker and SKIP LOCKED supports queue-like consumers [SRC-P20], but makes the team responsible for leases, recovery, fairness, retries and operations. It is a deliberate small-demo fallback, not a trivial reliable queue.

Gate: kill worker after claiming a task, restart broker, lose callback, submit duplicate request and test two workers. No lost business job; no repeated patch effect. Non-idempotent execution with uncertain completion becomes UNKNOWN/RECONCILE, never blindly retry. Enqueue short dispatch work; record long maintenance windows in PostgreSQL and recheck approvals at dispatch. If RabbitMQ resource/learning cost fails the actual laptop spike, use simpler durable dispatch with the same ledger; document the limitation. Do not add Kafka or Kubernetes to solve a workload not measured yet.

### P-D06 — Browser session + server-side permissions; OIDC seam
Recommend opaque, revocable server-side session identifiers in Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies for the same-origin dashboard, with CSRF protections for mutations, rotation and expiry. Use established authentication/session components, not custom cryptography [SRC-P21]. JWT is a token format, not an authorization model; long-lived browser localStorage tokens complicate theft/revocation. For external API clients/collectors, separate scoped short-lived credentials and rotation, not a reused human admin session.

Keycloak/OIDC offers centralized identity and standard flows [SRC-P24], appropriate when campus SSO, federation or multiple apps are required. It adds a server/database/configuration burden for five laptops; keep OIDC-compatible identity boundaries and adopt when justified. If application-auth implementation cannot meet reviewed security gates, Keycloak becomes preferable despite cost. No automatic assumption that rolling our own accounts is safer. Four confirmed roles: Administrator configures users/scopes; Analyst runs permitted scans and proposes remediation; Auditor reads allowed reports; Guest sees explicitly limited sanitized views. Patch approval/execution is a separately assigned permission and can require distinct proposer/approver. Deny by default, authorize every request and object; retrieval/tool calls inherit the same scope [SRC-P22].

### P-D07 — Separate execution authority and secrets
Runner pulls approved, typed jobs over an authenticated channel; use target IDs validated against authorized lab scopes, allowlisted adapter operations, bounded timeouts and resource limits. Do not interpolate a user's command or LLM output into a shell. Revalidate asset identity, target fingerprint, approved plan hash, expiration and current state immediately before mutation; changed evidence invalidates approval. [SRC-P23]

Credentials remain on the runner/secret store boundary wherever possible. API stores references, never returns cleartext secrets. Docker Compose secrets mount per-service files [SRC-P27]; this is not an encrypted vault or automatic rotation. Restrict host file permissions, keep secrets outside git/images, rotate/revoke after demos, and record access without values. Product-scale external secret manager is a later evaluated integration, not a claim that .env is sufficient [SRC-P28]. No Docker socket mount into the web API. Human approval is necessary but insufficient if the underlying target or plan changed.

### P-D08 — Compose on a Linux host; measured capacity and explicit backup
Docker documents single-server Compose deployment [SRC-P29]. Recommend a Linux lab host/VM with Compose profiles so DB/API/worker can run separately from expensive model/SIEM services. Do not require every student laptop to run the whole stack. Windows/macOS development is possible, but privileged network collection and VM networking need an early lab test. Docker Desktop education use is currently free under stated conditions; product/company use has separate conditions [SRC-P30]. Kubernetes offers cluster production management with additional control-plane, availability and security responsibilities [SRC-P31]; no known project requirement justifies that overhead now.

Do not invent RAM or cloud-price guarantees. Inventory actual RAM/CPU/storage/virtualization; measure cold start, typical job, peak ingestion and index build. Budget core demo around existing equipment and cached fixtures; cloud/paid LLM only after a current quote and spend cap. Keep a minimal offline demo profile plus a recorded fallback, clearly distinguish stale snapshot from live intelligence.

Initial raw evidence storage: private filesystem adapter on the single host, opaque content identifiers, metadata/hash/retention in PostgreSQL, size limits, no executable uploads and authenticated downloads. It is not scalable shared object storage. An S3 adapter is the future boundary if multiple hosts justify it. Do not select legacy MinIO by habit: its official repository says archived 25 Apr 2026 and no longer maintained [SRC-P32]. Its successor/commercial products are separate decisions, not automatically equivalent free replacements.

Back up DB, raw evidence, configuration and recovery keys as a consistent set. PostgreSQL documents SQL dumps, filesystem-level backup and continuous archiving [SRC-P33]; choose dump+evidence manifest for small demo, evaluate PITR for product deployment. Proposed demo targets RPO 24h and RTO 2h are assumptions to test, not existing guarantees. Restore onto a clean host before each discussion; snapshots on the same disk are not sufficient disaster recovery.

### P-D09 — Evidence-first operations and SIEM handoff
Structured events include event_id, correlation/job/attempt IDs, schema_version, actor, asset, advisory, evidence reference, severity/risk reasons, observed_at and status. Transactional outbox records state change and outbound event atomically; dispatcher retries with deduplication. Delivery acknowledgement is distinct from SIEM parsing/correlation success. Wazuh transport/decoder details belong in the collection integration memo; do not assume the Wazuh management API is a generic event ingestion API.

Application audit records and operational logs have different audiences and retention. Exclude passwords, raw tokens and unnecessary sensitive inventory from logs [SRC-P34]. Start with counters: ingestion lag, last success, failed source count, queue age, unknown findings, runner heartbeat, patch unknown/failure counts, assistant citation coverage, API latency and disk. OpenTelemetry provides Python instrumentation and traces [SRC-P35]; add collector/backend when troubleshooting distributed calls warrants it. A huge monitoring stack is optional, but fault visibility is core. Protect audit integrity; a database administrator can still alter ordinary audit tables, so do not claim immutable evidence without additional controls.

| P15 Security and fault evaluation / continuous then gates / 12–20h | Threat model + all modules → object authorization tests, input/command injection tests, denied runner actions, duplicate jobs, corrupt source and stale embedding tests → evidence report | Mahrous + Hams / P08,P11,P12 | No critical known authorization/unsafe execution issue at demo gate; all accepted residual risks documented; not a claim of comprehensive penetration certification |
| P16 Performance, accessibility and handover / term2 / 10–20h | Measured usage scenarios → benchmark declared asset/CVE counts, pagination/indexing; test keyboard/RTL; publish limitations, dependency/license inventory and operator docs → final release + reproducible benchmark | Shams + all / P10–P15 | Fresh teammate reproduces demo and benchmark; results state hardware/dataset; no invented enterprise-scale promise |

## Next-week Omar brief
By provisional 23 October: P01 complete, P02 schema examples agreed, P03 first migration, P05 one screen scaffold. Show faculty: a real API request and persisted record, role matrix, the dependency diagram, and which AI input/output is agreed with Hams. Do not promise all P03/P04 production hardening by this date. Platform work does not consume all AI capacity; early integration support is essential work.

## Architecture challenge / early stop conditions

1. If the laptop cannot run DB/API/worker alongside model/SIEM, split profiles across available machines before UI expansion. No unapproved cloud assumption.
2. If two modules disagree on identity/version semantics, stop feature work to repair P02; UI strings cannot repair corrupted matching semantics.
3. If role tests fail, no external pilot. “Private network” is not authorization.
4. If runner retry can repeat a patch, mutation remains disabled until attempt reconciliation is demonstrated.
5. If patch approval survives changed asset state, fix plan-hash/observation binding before automation.
6. If Hams model is unavailable, structured grounded recommendations and classifier baseline keep the slice useful; do not block all platform progress.
7. If schema and evidence backups restore independently but references break, the backup process fails acceptance.
8. If a single Omar-owned integration blocks everybody, pair one cyber member on contracts and one AI member on client integration; each critical component has a reviewer and handover note.
9. If feature velocity hides source staleness or unsupported devices, expose unknown/stale/unsupported as first-class statuses.
10. If a new dependency is unmaintained, licensing unclear, or cannot be pinned reproducibly, do not quietly add it for a demo. Record a replacement or postpone that capability.

# عقود التكامل وتصميم التنفيذ المشترك

Status: DESIGN DECISION / proposed v0. These are project contracts to implement and review in P02, not claims that the product already exists. Related decisions: ADR04, ADR08, ADR11, ADR12, ADR13, ADR18, ADR19. Public-source research informs mechanisms; payload names and enum choices below are our design.

## 1. One product, explicit boundaries

Browser → authenticated API → domain modules → PostgreSQL. A background worker consumes durable job IDs. A separately authenticated runner inside an authorized network executes allowlisted collection/patch operations. An inference process receives only authorized evidence and typed read-tool results. SIEM receives sanitized lifecycle events through the supported ingest route. The public planning website is only documentation; it is not a suitable host for privileged network scanning or the full product runtime.

Do not expose PostgreSQL, broker management ports, model server, or runner command endpoint to the public Internet. The exact reverse proxy/TLS/certificate implementation remains a deployment spike, because lab-only versus external pilot is not confirmed. No external pilot before that spike and authorization tests pass. Domain logic does not trust the browser or assistant. Authentication identifies the actor; authorization checks object, action and scope each time.

## 2. Repository and modules

Proposed product repository layout: backend/app/{inventory,intelligence,assessment,remediation,identity,ai_gateway,integrations}; runner/adapters/{ubuntu,windows}; frontend; contracts/v1; fixtures/{sources,inventory,matching,patch,assistant}; experiments; migrations; deploy; docs/{adr,runbooks,evaluation}. This layout is a recommendation, not an existing repository. Keep dependencies pinned with lockfiles. Choose exact supported stable versions after compatibility spike; do not pin an untested latest/nightly release from a website snippet.

Each module owns its model/service interface. API route handlers validate/authenticate then invoke domain logic. Shared contracts are versioned. Breaking schema change requires new version and migration. Fixture producers and consumers run contract tests before integration. Every PR states changed contract, expected behavior and relevant evidence; a reviewer from the consuming module checks it.

## 3. Canonical entities and initial constraints

| Entity | Required data / relationship | Integrity and query rule |
|---|---|---|
| Asset | UUID, organization/scope, owner, criticality, identity evidence, support profile | IP address is an observation; never the only stable identifier |
| Observation | asset, collected_at, method, collector version, raw evidence hash, OS/build/arch/package identities, errors, unknown fields | Immutable snapshot; freshness separate from import time |
| Source / source_revision | source URL, source ID, schema, external revision, fetched_at, source_modified_at, hash, terms link | Unique source+external ID+content hash; old revisions retained per policy |
| Vulnerability | internal UUID plus external IDs | Relationship types aliases/upstream/related are different; non-CVE is valid |
| Advisory assertion | source revision, product/range semantics, affected status, fixed/mitigation references | Multiple providers can disagree; retain both and conflict state |
| Assessment | asset snapshot, advisory revision, engine version, verdict, reason/evidence/gaps | Unique evaluation key; history append-only; current view derived |
| Priority | assessment, policy version, dated CVSS/KEV/EPSS, exposure and business reasons | Missing is not zero; internal priority separate from official severity |
| Patch plan | version, target manifest/hash, source fixes, expected observations, window, prechecks, recovery, reboot policy | One approved plan version; material change invalidates approval |
| Approval | plan hash, approver, scoped permission, time, expiry | API checks actor/action; runner independently checks executable plan validity |
| Job / attempt | logical job ID, idempotency key, operation, state, lease, heartbeat, attempts, result refs | Unique idempotency key; one mutation lease per asset; uncertain outcome reconciled |
| Outbox / audit | event ID, schema, actor, correlation, state change, evidence refs, delivery state | Outbox in transaction with business change; dedup at consumer; no secrets |
| Retrieval chunk | source revision, section/table identity, text hash, scope, embedding model/dimension | Derived and replaceable; stale chunk excluded from current answers |

Start indexes on exact external IDs, asset scope/last_seen, source modified/revision, assessment asset+state, and pending job dispatch. Add text/vector/JSON indexes only for measured queries. Use pagination and bounded exports. Preserve data on migration failure; a down migration cannot recreate dropped evidence.

## 4. API seams (proposed)

| Endpoint / operation | Actor and contract | Result |
|---|---|---|
| POST /v1/observations | Authorized collector/importer; InventorySnapshot | accepted observation ID or field-level validation error |
| GET /v1/assets/{id}/assessments | Scoped user | verdict, reason, evidence refs, freshness, unknown gaps |
| POST /v1/scan-jobs | Analyst within authorized scope; profile ID, target IDs, Idempotency-Key | 202 job ID; never accepts arbitrary command arguments |
| GET /v1/jobs/{id} | Scoped user | logical state + attempt timeline; partial failure visible |
| POST /v1/patch-plans | Remediation proposer; finding IDs + constraints | draft plan with unresolved prerequisites |
| POST /v1/patch-plans/{id}/approvals | Separate approval permission | version/hash-bound approval, expiry and actor |
| POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/dispatch | Authorized dispatcher after fresh policy check | queued execution; no direct browser→runner access |
| POST /v1/assistant/questions | Scoped user; question + selected asset IDs | answer, cited source spans, evidence version, uncertainty, suggested next evidence |
| GET /v1/source-health | Permitted analyst/admin; sanitized subset for others | last success, age, missing fields, failures and next retry |

Use consistent error envelope: code, message, correlation_id, retriable, field_errors. A timeout is distinct from denied, unsupported, source_stale and outcome_unknown. Return safe errors; internal stack traces never become user-facing evidence.

## 5. Worked payload — illustrative, not a real CVE or scan

```json
{
  "schema_version": "assessment.v1",
  "asset_id": "lab-example-01",
  "observation_id": "obs-example-07",
  "advisory_revision": "advisory-example-r2",
  "engine_version": "matching-example-v0",
  "verdict": "unknown",
  "reason_codes": ["MISSING_SOURCE_PACKAGE_VERSION"],
  "evidence_refs": ["evidence-example-03"],
  "gaps_to_collect": ["distribution_release", "source_package_version"],
  "evaluated_at": "2026-10-14T18:00:00Z"
}
```

C01/C03 and D02 define producer fields; P02 publishes schema; C05 and D05 produce independent evidence; D09 consumes both; C08 verifies the handoff; P06 displays the trace. Those are linked tasks, not duplicate matching implementations. C09 validates D14's catalog at the runner boundary rather than building another catalog. A10 and P11 share one assistant gateway implementation.

## 6. State machines and failure semantics

Assessment verdict: affected / not_affected / unknown / unsupported. Evidence freshness: current / stale / unavailable. Finding lifecycle: open / planned / execution_pending / verification_pending / resolved / risk_accepted / reopened. These are separate dimensions: a stale assessment is not “not affected”; a risk-accepted finding is not fixed.

Execution: queued → preflight → running → reboot_pending → verifying → succeeded. Any stage can become failed, canceled-before-mutation, or outcome_unknown. A canceled request does not magically undo a package change. outcome_unknown → reconcile → verified result or manual intervention. Campaign success requires every targeted asset's explicit result; partial outcomes remain partial.

Approval binds plan, target identity, evidence revision, time window and policy revision. Immediately before dispatch, compare current snapshot/target fingerprint. Expired or materially changed plan returns to draft/review. No tool or API path may jump from an assistant draft to execution.

## 7. Authorization matrix to agree before coding

| Action | Administrator | Analyst | Auditor | Guest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manage users / scopes | Yes | No | No | No |
| Run authorized read-only scans | Permission + scope | Permission + scope | No | No |
| Review evidence / triage | Scoped | Scoped | Allowed read-only reports | Sanitized allowed subset |
| Propose remediation | If assigned | If assigned | No | No |
| Approve / execute patch | Explicit additional permission; no implicit LLM delegation | Only if separately assigned by policy | No | No |
| Export sensitive inventory | Explicit scope/permission | Explicit scope/permission | Restricted report export | No |
| Ask assistant | Same underlying data/action permissions | Same underlying data/action permissions | Read-only permitted reports | Sanitized information only |

Two-person approval is a proposed default for mutation in the demonstrator; a documented single-operator lab exception must remain visibly distinct from production policy. Tests should include cross-asset access, revoked session, direct API access despite hidden UI, guessed object IDs and stale plan hash.

## 8. Observability, retention and release gates

Track ingestion lag, enrichment missingness, reassessment age, queue age, failed attempts, runner heartbeat, disk/RAM, unknown assessments, patch recovery, retrieval support and response latency. Each source has an owner and alert rule. Proposed first threshold: warn after two missed intended source polls; the 24h proposal requirement is separately measured and any miss reported.

Retention is a policy gate: no fixed legal retention claim is made. For lab planning, keep a compact immutable evaluation snapshot and all evidence needed to reproduce final reported results; limit noisy raw scans/LLM traces and remove secrets immediately. Record what was deleted, when and why. Before an external pilot decide inventory retention, user consent, access, export and deletion. Back up DB + evidence + keys/configuration as a consistent set; demonstrate restore. Proposed RPO24h/RTO2h must be measured, not assumed.

Release gate at each discussion: tagged commit; package/model/source version manifest; no secrets; known limitations; supported profile matrix; owner and independent reviewer; reproducible benchmark; backup restore; source outage and runner interruption demo. Security review uses selected versioned OWASP ASVS controls and NIST SSDF practices as guides, not a certification claim.

## 9. Future template readiness

Maintain requirements.csv mapping proposal IDs and later additions to tasks, owner, metric and proof artifact. Keep an assumptions log, ADRs, risk register, source licenses and research protocol. For the faculty template, fill the approved formal roster only after the Shams/Shahd discrepancy is resolved. Keep original proposal untouched; a new requirement is marked addition, and a changed target requires supervisor agreement.

Primary references: [OWASP ASVS](https://owasp.org/projects/asvs), [NIST SSDF](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final), [SEI architecture risk](https://www.sei.cmu.edu/library/managing-architectural-risk-during-agile-development/). Specific framework/queue/security mechanism references are in the platform source register; contracts above are our proposed implementation design.

# Scope revision — evidence, alternatives and execution gates

Revision 2026-10-23.r2 applies the 22 October meeting and the later on-prem correction. The original five research chapters and 97 source entries remain available with their original dates. This chapter adds targeted evidence; it does not claim new experiments or customer interviews have happened.

## What is confirmed, proposed and unknown

**Confirmed team requirements:** Hams leads UI/UX research/design as well as AI; Omar implements the frontend/platform. Each person needs owned work and supporting work separately. On-prem is a required long-term product direction, with enabling foundations now. The current request authorizes editing the planning site, not creating or updating ClickUp tickets.

**Recommended delivery scope:** IT infrastructure supporting industrial operations: one qualified Ubuntu release for real lab remediation, plus a conditional FortiOS advisory/import profile for matching and reviewed recommendations. This is a project recommendation, not proven customer fit, a signed customer contract or permission to access an industrial company. Actual hardware, installation access, budget, model quality and existing work progress remain unknown.

**Unsupported claim:** the meeting's “90% caused by people” is not research evidence. Do not repeat it as a fact, use it as a label, or equate recurring findings with employee fault.

## Scope comparison and restrictions

| Option | Practical advantage | Main implementation burden | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| General enterprise IT | Broad need and several public sources | Multiple OS/package/version, collection and update semantics | Preserve extension work; do not commit all profiles now |
| Network appliances only | Clear vendor advisory and upgrade decision problem | Model/train/config evidence, hardware access, entitlement and recovery | Qualify one recommendation-only FortiOS profile |
| IT supporting industrial operations | Can demonstrate a real Ubuntu lifecycle with maintenance/business context | Customer-fit hypothesis and accurate scope wording | Recommended next release |
| Direct OT | Potential specialist value | Safety, reliability, protocols, equipment and vendor qualification | Separate future gate; no generic probing or firmware execution |

NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 addresses OT's distinct operational constraints. Its publication page currently points to an initial draft of Revision 4; that draft is not substituted for the final baseline. Our scope recommendation follows from these constraints plus the team's resources; NIST does not endorse our chosen product segment. [MR05]

A device does not need internet exposure to be assessed. A local runner still needs authorized reachability, a supported protocol, sufficient credentials and reliable identity/version/configuration evidence. Fragile or isolated equipment may permit only a vendor-approved export or manual evidence. An import cannot create missing configuration facts: its timestamp, origin and unknown fields must remain visible. Discovery, inventory, assessment, recommendation and execution are separate capabilities. See C01/C03/C07 and the profile matrix.

## Fortinet profile: a feasibility gate, not a new patch engine

Fortinet's official feed guide distinguishes PSIRT advisories and public RSS from support-login bulletins and firmware downloads. The PSIRT interface contains product/version advisories and the vendor provides an upgrade-path tool. Endpoint availability and commercial redistribution rights still need D17/D18 validation. A publicly readable page is not automatically a licensed product feed. [MR06] [MR07] [MR08]

D17 should retrieve a small reproducible sample, retain revisions, and qualify structured CSAF access when available. If retrieval is blocked, preserve a documented manual-review route without bypassing access restrictions. RSS discovery alone cannot prove that every advisory revision was collected. Record advisory ID, product/train, affected ranges, configuration prerequisites, fixed-branch assertions and one-to-many CVE links.

A fixed release listed in an advisory is distinct from a safe end-to-end upgrade path. Hardware support, release notes, prerequisites, maintenance window, backup and tested intermediate steps still matter. Never interpret “fixed in X” as “jump directly to latest.” The current profile produces reviewed recommendations, not automatic FortiOS firmware execution. Do not promote unverified version examples from earlier notes into gold labels. D14 remains the single remediation catalog; D09 remains the single applicability engine.

## Top ten: compare units before ranking

| Unit | Useful for | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| Unique CVEs | Source-level awareness and threat trend views | Hides affected asset count and actual work |
| Asset–vulnerability findings | Evidence and per-asset applicability | Many findings may share one compatible fix |
| Grouped remediation actions | Analyst execution queue | Unsafe if grouping crosses incompatible versions, windows or policy |

Use up to ten eligible compatible actions as the primary queue, with per-finding and CVE drill-down. This is a design recommendation. D12 must define grouping keys, eligibility, deterministic tie-breaking and reason codes. Keep unknown applicability, missing context, no-patch and maintenance-blocked states visible. Do not turn a policy score into a calibrated probability of compromise. Existing KEV, EPSS and CVSS research still governs their different meanings.

A15 compares CVSS-only, explained policy and grouped-action views on the same frozen cases. Use independently reviewed ranking judgments, justify relevance labels before using precision@10 or nDCG@10, and report duplicate workload, unsafe actions, missed urgent cases and analyst task time. Do not claim a market-leading result from a small lab or an incomparable competitor trial.

Recurrence must distinguish an unchanged observation, evidence aging, an advisory correction, reopening after verified closure and actual confirmed drift. A root-cause hypothesis requires a reviewer and supporting evidence before becoming confirmed. A repeated CVE alone does not prove the cause, and synthetic histories are not customer incident evidence. L&D or game mechanics remain future intervention hypotheses.

## AI: organization context without a foundation-model project

The retained design combines structured facts, governed retrieval and constrained generation. The database holds source assertions, assets, assessments, ranking policy and live lifecycle state. Derived retrieval indexes contain source text and scoped explanatory documents, with links back to versions. Current object-level facts come through authorized tools. Organization context includes owner, criticality, exposure, policy revision, maintenance restrictions and recorded history. Missing fields stay missing; they are not inferred from CVE prose.

The SecBERT publisher presents a cybersecurity BERT model. It can be evaluated as an encoder/classification candidate with an appropriate task head; it is not a drop-in conversational model. Exact artifact/license and a fair downstream benchmark are A05/D18 gates. [MR10]

“API” describes an interface, not who hosts it. An internal on-prem inference service can expose an API. Some hosted model services support supervised tuning, so the blanket statement “an API model cannot be trained” is incorrect. No hosted provider or tuned model is selected by this correction. Current knowledge is handled through ingestion, retrieval and tools; fine-tuning needs a separate justified task, rights-cleared labels, cost/privacy review and measured benefit. [MR11]

The assistant workflow authorizes scope, reads facts, retrieves permitted evidence, drafts or abstains, validates support and returns a cited answer. Applicability, priority policy, approval and dispatch remain outside model authority. Begin with explicit typed application state and the existing durable job boundary. LangGraph offers persistence and human oversight and can work without LangChain; adopt it only if the required resume/state behavior justifies the extra integration and maintenance burden. No cloud tracing service is implied. [MR09]

Model outage must degrade to cited deterministic cards/templates. Source outage uses a visibly stale trusted snapshot. Neither authorizes silently forwarding organization data to a different provider.

## Data plan and realistic gaps

| Need | Preferred evidence | Honest limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Vulnerability assertions | Official CVE and vendor records, NVD enrichment | No source proves all installed assets are affected |
| Threat signals | Retained KEV/EPSS integrations | Signals are dated and have distinct meanings |
| Asset behavior and repairs | Authorized real lab observations before/after mutation | Lab results are not production reliability statistics |
| Organization context | Consented policies/inventory if available | Public sources do not supply this organization's current context |
| Controlled context scenarios | Explicitly synthetic policies/assets/histories | Useful fixtures, not real-world performance evidence |
| Ranking/answer labels | Reviewed independent judgments with disagreement recorded | No universal public organization-specific ranking ground truth |

A02 records origin, source/rights, revision, hashes and split. A03 groups duplicates/revisions before splitting. D15 uses reviewed expected outcomes independent of the evaluated rules/model. Kaggle may point to a candidate dataset but is not a source guarantee; audit upstream provenance, license, duplication, schema and representativeness. LLM-generated CVEs or fixed versions must never replace authoritative assertions. Report real-record, real-lab and synthetic-scenario denominators separately.

## On-prem: how and when

On-prem is a required product direction, not the fallback if cloud fails. Design for it now and qualify it in stages. Some customers accept cloud; a universal “companies reject cloud/APIs” claim is unsupported. Deployment and procurement requirements must be elicited for the intended customers.

| Approach | Fits | Costs / risks | Project position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cloud app + approved external inference | Fast shared demos where privacy/terms permit | Recurring cost, egress, retention, network dependence | Optional deployment, no provider chosen |
| Customer-hosted core + approved external inference | Keeps core storage local when policy permits inference egress | Still not disconnected or fully local | Explicit hybrid capability profile only |
| Connected on-prem + local inference | Local data/model boundary with controlled updates | Hardware, operators, backups and model quality | First product qualification milestone |
| Disconnected on-prem | Environments needing no runtime public egress | Bundle supply chain, freshness, packages and lifecycle cost | Required staged direction; qualify after connected profile |

Docker documents single-server Compose deployment with environment-specific overrides. This supports extending the retained deployment approach; it does not establish high availability, secure customer operation or any minimum hardware figure. [MR02]

Ollama provides a local-runtime route with networking/cloud controls. Hams must benchmark the actual model, context, concurrency and hardware, disable cloud features for the local profile, and test outbound behavior. A local model alone does not make the entire application offline: embeddings, tokenizer downloads, identity, telemetry, source sync, package repositories and fonts can still depend on the network. [MR01]

1. **G0–G1 foundations — P01/P02/D18/A06/P11.** Measure available hosts. Version domain/context contracts and provider/update adapters. Keep database/evidence local-capable; separate configuration, credentials and artifact locations from domain logic. Inventory enabled dependencies and egress. Do not introduce Kubernetes or a second control plane simply to anticipate scale.
2. **G2 connected on-prem — P14/A09.** Install the qualified core plus local inference on a measured lab/customer-like host. Use private service networking and an isolated runner. Test local identity, secret rotation, restart, approved update routes and consistent database/evidence restore. Record exact capacity and disabled capabilities.
3. **G3 disconnected — P17.** Stage trusted versioned artifacts on a connected machine. Export images, models/tokenizers, embeddings, source snapshots, config templates, migrations and notices. Supply secrets separately. Import on a clean compatible host with public egress blocked. Test enabled workflows, tampered/incompatible bundles and recovery. A disabled assistant is a labelled degraded mode, not a full-AI offline pass.
4. **After pilot, customer qualification.** Validate required SSO/PKI, retention, update cadence, incident/support process, sizing and availability. Multi-host/HA deployment is a separate measured requirement. No dates or customer approvals are fabricated.

Docker image save/load moves images; data/model volumes need separate handling. Checksums detect alteration relative to a trusted manifest but do not establish who produced it. Before the disconnected release, qualify offline-verifiable publisher authentication or a documented trusted transfer process and key handling. [MR03] [MR04]

A disconnected system cannot guarantee upstream publication-to-usable freshness while no update enters it. Show source as-of/import age and overdue update warnings. Offline patching additionally needs approved available package content, metadata and dependencies; a local CVE snapshot does not provide those packages. Preserve the connected 24-hour proposal target with a clear deployment-mode denominator.

There is no promise of “never change the base.” Stable contracts, adapters, capability flags, fixture compatibility and versioned migrations reduce avoidable rewrites while allowing necessary evolution.

## Team and ticket handoff

Hams sequences UX01/A01, dataset provenance/splits, then the minimum UX02 handoff, CPU baseline and scoped corpus according to weekly capacity. A07/A09 come after their inputs; stronger classifiers and rerankers remain conditional. Omar builds the fixture shell during design research, then implements the reviewed P05 flow. UX03 tests the implementation and produces correction issues.

Before ticket import, reconcile actual existing artifacts against one scope/schema/fixture manifest. Mahrous and Hams agree on applicability outputs, user questions and organization-context fields; Omar validates contract consumption, Shams provenance/rights and Amr collection feasibility. If work is missing or incompatible, record the exact gap and owner. The website does not know Mohamed's completion state. The CSV is prepared guidance with full execution descriptions and links; nothing is synchronized or sent to ClickUp by this update.

## Architecture challenge and early cautions

| Failure scenario | Early experiment / response | Owner / package |
|---|---|---|
| Scope drift makes AI consume different verdicts | Reconcile one case against the shared manifest before model work | Mahrous + Hams / P02 |
| Hams is overloaded by UX and AI | Limit simultaneous work; minimal design handoff and CPU baseline first | Hams / UX01–03, A04 |
| Fortinet feed/terms cannot be qualified | Small sample gate before a broad adapter commitment; retain Ubuntu core | Shams / D17/D18 |
| Grouping hides an incompatible upgrade | Constraint fixtures and reviewed grouping outputs | Mahrous / D12 |
| Root-cause narrative becomes unsupported blame | Separate hypotheses and confirmed causes with evidence | Mahrous / D13; Hams / A11 |
| Local model exceeds hardware | Early measured A09 domain/context/concurrency spike | Hams + Omar / A09/P01 |
| “Offline” startup fetches a hidden dependency | Clean-host blocked-egress install and endpoint log review | Omar / P17 |
| Update breaks database/evidence links | Versioned compatibility gate, backup and replay/restore test | Omar / P14/P17 |
| Public data is treated as commercially redistributable | Tool/data/model rights matrix before relevant release | Shams / D18 |
| UI looks finished but misleads on approval/unknown | Frozen tasks, observed decisions and exception-state review | Hams + Omar / UX02/UX03 |

These risks extend the retained register. They are qualitative planning concerns, not measured incident probabilities. New hard dependency UX02 → P05 gates the finished UI handoff; shell exploration can run earlier. D17 does not block the Ubuntu engine. P17 qualifies a later deployment capability and does not block the first real lab slice. Other existing engine/catalog/gateway ownership boundaries remain intact.

decisions.title: قرار التأثر
decisions.choice: Deterministic vendor-aware engine بثلاث حالات
decisions.why: affected/not_affected/unknown مع مقارنة versions ودليل وشروط.
decisions.alternatives: LLM/fuzzy candidate generation أوسع لكنه غير موثوق كحكم؛ exploit validation ليس شرطًا عامًا.
decisions.gate: D09 + C08 + D15: gold fixtures مع backport/config missing وprecision/recall.
decisions.risk: الخطأ في ecosystem comparator أخطر من اختيار model ضعيف.
decisions.fallback: Unknown + targeted evidence request + analyst review.

decisions.title: تحديد الأولوية
decisions.choice: Policy bands تفسيرية: KEV + exposure + criticality + CVSS + dated EPSS
decisions.why: كل إشارة لها معنى؛ EPSS forecast وCVSS severity ليستا risk score محليًا.
decisions.alternatives: Weighted score baseline ممكن؛ learned ranking يحتاج labels؛ SSVC يساعد decision tree لكنه يحتاج سياق المؤسسة.
decisions.gate: D12: حالات متعارضة وmissing signals ومراجعة supervisor policy.
decisions.risk: KEV absence لا تعني no exploitation؛ non-CVE لا يملك EPSS؛ لا threshold عالمي.
decisions.fallback: Manual priority مع reasons وreview date.

decisions.title: Discovery & inventory
decisions.choice: Nmap مستقل محدود + native SSH Ubuntu؛ agent Windows بعد مقارنة
decisions.why: Discovery يكتشف endpoints؛ authenticated collection يثبت packages/builds.
decisions.alternatives: osquery أخف نسبيًا لكن يحتاج transport؛ Wazuh ممتاز إن موجود؛ Greenbone أثقل ومفيد validation اختياري.
decisions.gate: C01–C06: scope/identity/permissions/footprint على الأجهزة الفعلية.
decisions.risk: NPSL/Npcap redistribution؛ active probes fragile devices؛ privilege drift.
decisions.fallback: Signed export/manual inventory بإظهار freshness.

decisions.title: Patch execution
decisions.choice: نبني orchestration ونستخدم native managers عبر allowlisted Ansible adapter
decisions.why: القيمة في applicability، approvals، recovery والتحقق، لا إعادة بناء package manager.
decisions.alternatives: Native direct أبسط dependency لكن نملك parsing/reboots؛ commercial integrations لاحقًا عند availability.
decisions.gate: C11–C13: Ubuntu canary + interruption + restore؛ Windows C14 بعد gate مستقل.
decisions.risk: GPL/collection terms؛ check-mode لا يثبت compatibility؛ لا rollback عام.
decisions.fallback: Manual approved execution + fresh evidence، أو no mutation.

decisions.title: Backend boundary
decisions.choice: Python modular monolith + منفذ privileged منفصل
decisions.why: يقلل integration cost ويحافظ على boundary للمهام الخطرة.
decisions.alternatives: Microservices تعقيد deployment/observability مبكر؛ فصل كل module ليس scalability مثبتة.
decisions.gate: P02/P08: typed contracts؛ API/LLM لا ينفذ shell؛ runner rejects invalid scope.
decisions.risk: Single host failure؛ module coupling؛ privilege escalation.
decisions.fallback: تخفيض profile وتشغيل manual lab؛ فصل service لاحقًا عند قياس bottleneck.

decisions.title: Backend framework
decisions.choice: FastAPI candidate؛ Django أقوى بديل
decisions.why: Python/OpenAPI contracts تسهل AI/data؛ القرار يحترم مهارة Omar الفعلية.
decisions.alternatives: Django يوفر auth/admin أكثر؛ NestJS مناسب TS قوي لكنه يزيد Python boundary.
decisions.gate: P01: endpoint+migration في يومي عمل مركزين كحد تجريبي؛ auth component review قبل اعتماد framework.
decisions.risk: FastAPI لا يوفر نظام مستخدمين كاملًا؛ السرعة النظرية لا تثبت workload.
decisions.fallback: Django أو stack يتقنه Omar مع نفس contracts.

decisions.title: Frontend
decisions.choice: React + TypeScript + Vite SPA
decisions.why: Dashboard خاص يحتاج data/state أكثر من SEO؛ نفس origin مع API.
decisions.alternatives: Next.js قوي لو server rendering/SSO integrations أو خبرة Omar ترجحه؛ vanilla UI للـplanning site فقط وليس قرار backend المنتج.
decisions.gate: P05: keyboard/RTL/error/loading مع fixture ثم real endpoint.
decisions.risk: Routing/data cache dependencies إضافية؛ تحقق versions والصيانة عند spike.
decisions.fallback: واجهة محدودة بلا polish زائد أو stack مثبت للفريق.

decisions.title: Database & retrieval
decisions.choice: PostgreSQL relational + JSONB؛ pgvector بعد benchmark
decisions.why: الـjoins والتاريخ والصلاحيات وsearch في نظام واحد؛ canonical ≠ vector.
decisions.alternatives: MySQL JSON صالح لو خبرة أقوى؛ Qdrant لاحقًا إن scale/filtering justify خدمة ثانية.
decisions.gate: P03/A07: duplicate/revision integrity، filtered recall، restore وquery plan.
decisions.risk: ANN recall/memory؛ indexing JSON عشوائي؛ RLS superuser bypass.
decisions.fallback: Lexical/exact search أولًا؛ isolate retrieval adapter.

decisions.title: Durable jobs
decisions.choice: Postgres job ledger/outbox؛ Celery + RabbitMQ أول تجربة broker
decisions.why: الدليل التجاري لحالة job لا يعتمد على memory أو worker callback.
decisions.alternatives: Redis/RQ أبسط إن جاهز لكن visibility/license matters؛ DB-only يقلل خدمات لكنه يحملنا leases/recovery.
decisions.gate: E04/P07: duplicate/crash/broker restart/reconcile + measured RAM.
decisions.risk: At-least-once ≠ exactly-once؛ repeated side effects؛ broker learning cost.
decisions.fallback: Bounded serial worker مع durable ledger وmanual reconcile؛ لا in-process BackgroundTasks كضمان.

decisions.title: Authentication
decisions.choice: Server-side revocable cookie sessions + per-object permissions
decisions.why: نطاق نفس origin وأربعة أدوار؛ JWT وحده لا يحل authorization.
decisions.alternatives: Keycloak/OIDC أفضل لو SSO أو app-auth gate يفشل؛ يزيد operations. Short-lived scoped tokens للـrunner/API منفصلة.
decisions.gate: P04: CSRF/session rotation/logout/denial matrix؛ مراجعة component maintained قبل code.
decisions.risk: XSS/CSRF أو role bypass؛ لا custom crypto؛ secret storage ليس .env فقط.
decisions.fallback: Identity provider عند الحاجة؛ لا external pilot قبل gate.

decisions.title: Infrastructure & evidence
decisions.choice: Compose Linux single host/profiles + private filesystem evidence adapter
decisions.why: يتناسب مع 5طلاب وميزانية محدودة؛ نقيس الأجهزة ولا نطلب cloud تلقائيًا.
decisions.alternatives: Kubernetes بعد حاجة تشغيل حقيقية؛ managed cloud بعد quote؛ S3 عندما multi-host يبرر؛ MinIO legacy archived.
decisions.gate: P14: clean setup/restore/resource profile؛ determine TLS/cert/deployment network قبل pilot.
decisions.risk: Single point failure؛ disk capacity؛ Desktop terms؛ backups في نفس disk غير كافية.
decisions.fallback: Minimal offline profile + replay معلن؛ فصل model/SIEM على جهاز آخر.

decisions.title: ML classification
decisions.choice: TF-IDF word/char + OneVsRest baseline؛ multilabel category/impact
decisions.why: سريع ومفسر ويؤسس مقارنة علمية قبل model أعقد.
decisions.alternatives: Frozen embeddings plus a linear head may be compared with the baseline. Pretrained encoder fine-tuning is outside the current release; revisit only through OQ01.
decisions.gate: A01–A05: dedup/group/time split؛ no label-derived leakage؛ macro/microF1.
decisions.risk: Imbalance/missing labels/pretrained contamination؛ severity inference ليست official CVSS.
decisions.fallback: Baseline موثق + abstention؛ قلل taxonomy غير القابلة للمراجعة.

decisions.title: RAG
decisions.choice: Exact IDs + lexical + multilingual dense حسب التجربة
decisions.why: استرجاع أدلة حديثة مع metadata/revision/scope، وليس حفظ CVEs في model weights.
decisions.alternatives: E5-small مقابل BGE-M3؛ MiniLM comparator؛ reranker فقط إذا ranking bottleneck؛ vector-only يضيع exact facts.
decisions.gate: A06–A08: Recall@k/nDCG/Arabic+Arabizi والـRAM؛ لا خلط version-table rows.
decisions.risk: Stale chunks؛ embeddings spaces تختلف؛ authorization filters قد تقلل ANN recall.
decisions.fallback: Exact+lexical cited cards؛ لا إسقاط scope filter لتحسين recall.

decisions.title: Customized LLM
decisions.choice: Domain tools+retrieval+schema أولًا؛ Qwen candidates vs Gemma في spike
decisions.why: التخصيص يبدأ بسلوك موثق وأدوات محدودة؛ لا نعيد التدريب لكل CVE.
decisions.alternatives: Qwen3.5-4B Apache2 مقابل Qwen3 Instruct أبسط؛ Gemma3 شروط مختلفة؛ cloud مشروط privacy/cost research.
decisions.gate: A09: نفس60سؤال reviewed، actual hardware/context/quantization/runtime؛ no winner قبل النتائج.
decisions.risk: RAM/context/tool output errors؛ modelcard benchmarks ليست domain proof؛ remote code/download risk.
decisions.fallback: Use cited deterministic explanations if generative support is inadequate. Fine-tuning is outside current implementation; any future proposal must satisfy OQ01.

decisions.title: Assistant authority
decisions.choice: Read-only scoped tools + validated answer؛ draft منفصل عن approve/execute
decisions.why: المساعد يشرح current facts ويطلب missing evidence؛ لا يمتلك مفاتيح تنفيذ.
decisions.alternatives: Autonomous unrestricted agent يزيد attack surface؛ prompt-only guardrails غير كافية.
decisions.gate: A10–A12/P11: indirect injection/cross-role/fake citations/stale-plan suite.
decisions.risk: RAG لا يلغي prompt injection؛ JSON صحيح قد يكون كاذبًا.
decisions.fallback: Disable assistant واحتفظ workflow الأساسي.

decisions.title: SIEM & monitoring
decisions.choice: Outbox → JSON lines → Wazuh agent decoder/rules؛ counters أولًا
decisions.why: يثبت وصول الحدث وفهمه؛ source/queue/runner health جزء core.
decisions.alternatives: Generic management REST ليس event ingest؛ full observability stack يضاف حسب الحاجة؛ OTel option بعد tracing need.
decisions.gate: C15/P13: event_id موحد في DB وSIEM alert؛ duplicate/replay/rotation test.
decisions.risk: Loss/duplicates/log secrets؛ database audit ليست tamper-proof تلقائيًا.
decisions.fallback: Replayable export معلن؛ لا نسميه integrated حتى تظهر alert.

decisions.title: ما يميز المشروع
decisions.choice: اختبر change-aware decisions + targeted evidence + constrained remediation
decisions.why: قيمة يمكن قياسها في correctness/time/effort ضمن نطاق محدود.
decisions.alternatives: Chatbot/approvals/patch integrations وحدها ليست novelty؛ Tenable Hexa يوثقها بالفعل.
decisions.gate: A15/D15: same fixtures/source snapshot؛ ablations وnegative results؛ competitor access إن متاح.
decisions.risk: Academic usefulness بدون usability أو usability بدون contribution؛ ادعاء تفوق بلا benchmark.
decisions.fallback: Research contribution أضيق قابل للإثبات مع limitations صريحة.

decisions.why: General IT is broad; direct OT requires equipment and safety qualification; appliance-only execution adds entitlement/hardware risk.

Five members, three domains, a yearlong graduation project, four discussions, plus later patch/RAG/assistant additions.
Proposal targets
24-hour CVE freshness; at least 90% detection in a declared controlled lab; at least 90% clear/actionable recommendations; four roles and SIEM. These are targets, not measured results.
Calendar assumption
23 October 2026 is a provisional internal role-review target. Official discussion dates still need confirmation.
Resources unknown
The proposal lists five laptops and a historical 1,500 EGP budget. Actual hardware, weekly hours, Windows lab access and recurring spend are unconfirmed.
Roster check
Use the working name Shams; confirm the PDF roster discrepancy before filling an official template.
Skills and choices
Ownership follows the team descriptions. Exact framework skills, model suitability and infrastructure choices require the named experiments.
Naming
AegisLoop is the product name; Vector Five is the team name. Availability/trademark checks have not been performed. The historical proposal retains its original title.

researchQuestions.label: Research
added: What does CVE.org provide versus NVD enrichment?

implementationSteps.label: Build steps
added: Create vulnerability-intelligence/ and a README with the sample command, Python environment, input CVE list and output locations. Keep API credentials outside the repository.

Choose 10–20 published representative CVEs: complete and missing-score records, amended/rejected cases where available, several product types, affected ranges and missing fixed-version information. Save the selection rationale.

Read the retained CVE and NVD source documentation. Record the exact official retrieval mechanism, authentication, current quota evidence, update behavior and usage/attribution conditions in research/source-comparison.md. Mark unverifiable limits as unresolved.
Implement collectors/cve_org.py to fetch each selected official CVE record. Preserve the untouched response plus source URL, retrieved_at, status, source revision/schema and content hash in raw/.

Implement collectors/nvd.py to fetch the same CVE IDs from NVD. Preserve NVD responses separately; log missing enrichment or failed requests without replacing the CVE record or advancing a false success marker.
Compare identifiers, descriptions, dates, scores, affected products/ranges, CPE, references and remediation fields. Document which assertions are provider-specific, missing or conflicting.

Draft schema/vulnerability-schema-v0.1.json with internal/external IDs, separate provider assertions, raw revision references, affected-range semantics, source timestamps and explicit missing fields. This draft is input to D02, not the final shared schema.

Build normalizers/sample.py to combine references to both raw records into normalized sample objects without silently choosing a winner for conflicting fields. Do not derive fixed versions from guesswork.
Write normalized/samples.jsonl and raw/manifest.json. Validate every selected sample against the draft schema and preserve partial cases with clear errors or missing-field flags.
Repeat the process from saved raw files, then ask Mahrous/Omar to run the README and review the field comparison. Save successful and failed test results before handing the prototype to D02 and D03.

researchQuestions.label: Research
added: What hostname, public or private DNS and certificate issuer are appropriate for the qualified demo or customer-hosted profile?
Where will TLS terminate, which proxy headers are trusted and how is certificate renewal tested?
Which exact inbound, service-to-service and outbound connections are required; which services must have no public listener?
How are database/evidence/model volumes, off-host backup, secrets and migration recovery handled?
Who deploys, monitors, updates, restores and pays for each enabled environment?

implementationSteps.label: Build steps
added: Use P01 measurements to write deployment/hosting-plan.md: selected location, host/OS/runtime, administrator, permitted users, capacity evidence, estimated recurring cost and limits. Keep exact provider, size and proxy choice Needs Validation until the comparison passes.

Document each component placement and connection: UI/TLS entry, API, worker/job ledger, PostgreSQL, evidence volumes, model/embedding endpoint and isolated runner. Separate the public HTTPS entry, private services and authorized target network; do not publish database, broker, model or runner listeners as internet endpoints.

Create a staging configuration with fixture data and a restricted demo/pilot configuration. Pin release/image versions and provide a configuration template with placeholder values only; provision runtime secrets separately.

Configure the selected hostname/DNS and TLS termination route after the environment gate. Compare the already-supported proxy approaches and pick one through a small test; public certificate automation and private/on-prem certificate trust have different validation and renewal requirements. Trust forwarded headers only from the configured proxy boundary.

Test inbound and outbound connectivity from approved and denied locations; document host firewall/container port mappings, allowed source updates and runner-to-target reachability. A cloud application does not automatically reach private customer devices.

Attach persistence and coordinated backup/restore jobs for database, evidence and required configuration/key recovery; keep protected backups on separate authorized storage and record measured recovery objectives. A recreated container or same-disk snapshot is not a complete recovery plan.

Write a release procedure: verify build/tests, take a recoverable backup, apply a compatible migration, deploy pinned artifacts, run smoke/health checks and stop or recover on failure. Do not assume that rolling an image back reverses a destructive database migration.

Define startup/readiness checks, restart behavior, disk/backup/certificate-age warnings, sanitized logs and responsible contacts. Have Amr reproduce a clean deployment and restore; document failed steps before the P14 handoff.

after: Freeze the C03 enrolled-ID baseline and reviewer-labelled conflict cases before changing rules.

goal.label: goal

study.purpose: A personal reference for understanding, explaining and discussing AegisLoop. This is a static learning layer, not a team progress tracker.

chapters.title: Know what the sources actually tell us
chapters.question: How does a published advisory become evidence we can use?
chapters.ar: المصدر بيقول إيه؟ وإيه اللي لسه مش نعرفه عن الجهاز؟
takeaways: Preserve raw source records before normalization; CVE, NVD and vendor assertions may add different facts.
The internal schema preserves identities, revisions, conflicts and missing fields.
A vendor fix statement is evidence for a product branch, not permission to update every device.
chapters.trap: A CVE appearing in the database does not establish that one of our assets is affected.
chapters.ask: Explain why D03 does not have to wait for all NVD enrichment in D04.

chapters.title: Know the asset before judging it
chapters.question: What facts must we collect from an authorized device?
chapters.ar: الجهاز عنده إيه فعلًا، والمعلومة اتجمعت إمتى ومنين؟
takeaways: Approved scope and stable identity come before collection. An IP alone is insufficient.
Ubuntu inventory needs the distribution and full package revision, not just an old-looking banner.
An import is a valid evidence path when its origin, age and limitations are disclosed.
chapters.trap: Network discovery, authenticated inventory and vulnerability assessment are different capabilities.
chapters.ask: If a firmware export lacks model/configuration evidence, what can we safely conclude?

chapters.title: Understand applicability and priority
chapters.question: Is this asset affected, and which action matters first?
chapters.ar: متأثر فعلًا؟ وبعد كده نبدأ بإيه وليه؟
takeaways: D09 applies vendor-aware rules and returns affected, not_affected or unknown with a trace.
D12 uses distinct threat/context signals; severity alone is not the work queue.
Revisions and new observations can change an earlier result; D13 preserves reassessment and history.
A17 tests AI/hybrid ordering against D12 policy; models cannot change applicability or permission constraints.
chapters.trap: Unknown is not safe. EPSS, CVSS and KEV do not mean the same thing.
chapters.ask: Explain why a fixed backport can defeat a simple comparison of upstream version numbers.

chapters.title: Separate what AI learns, retrieves and explains
chapters.question: Where does the assistant add value without becoming a security authority?
chapters.ar: التصنيف غير البحث، والبحث غير الحكم على الجهاز، والشرح غير التنفيذ.
takeaways: Classification needs defined labels, real provenance and leakage-safe evaluation.
RAG retrieves governed source/policy text; typed tools obtain current authorized system facts.
Hams leads AI and UX design. Omar implements the product UI and the shared API gateway.
chapters.trap: An embedding match or fluent answer is not an applicability verdict or an approval.
chapters.ask: How can new CVE knowledge become usable without retraining the generative model?

chapters.title: Follow a repair through to verified closure
chapters.question: What makes a patch action controlled and its result credible?
chapters.ar: مش مجرد أمر اشتغل؛ لازم نعرف اتصلّح إيه وحالة الخدمة إيه.
takeaways: A reviewed plan binds the targets, source/observation revisions, permissions and recovery constraints.
The runner is isolated from the web API and LLM; lost contact can mean outcome_unknown.
Fresh independent collection and service checks establish closure; a command exit code does not.
chapters.trap: A newer release is not always a compatible upgrade, and reconnecting is not permission to repeat a mutation.
chapters.ask: What must happen if the network disappears after package installation starts?

chapters.title: Understand the platform and hosting boundaries
chapters.question: How do the pieces work together without competing sources of truth?
chapters.ar: الـplatform بيربط الأجزاء؛ مش بيعمل حكم تاني يناقضهم.
takeaways: P02 combines the domain contracts; P03 stores structured facts, revisions and relationships.
P04/P08 separate user permissions from runner authority; P07 makes jobs durable.
P14 qualifies connected hosting. P17 separately qualifies disconnected installation and updates.
chapters.trap: An internal API is compatible with on-prem. This public planning site is not the deployed vulnerability-management product.
chapters.ask: Why does putting Ollama on localhost not prove that the entire application works offline?

case.title: Read the advisory
case.input: A fictional advisory DEMO-ADV-A, its original source and revision.
case.action: Preserve raw evidence and normalize provider assertions without inventing a missing fixed version.
case.output: A versioned advisory object linked to its raw record.
case.because: We need to know exactly which source assertion later reasoning used.
case.question: Does this advisory alone prove that asset LAB-A is affected?
case.answer: No. We still need asset identity, installed versions and any required configuration evidence.

case.title: Observe the asset
case.owner: Shams; Mahrous defines the observation fields
case.input: Authorized fictional Ubuntu asset LAB-A and an approved collection profile.
case.action: Collect distribution/release, package identity/full revision and timestamp with errors stated explicitly.
case.output: A stable asset observation; missing required configuration remains missing.
case.because: A banner or IP cannot substitute for installed package and platform identity.
case.question: What if the observation contains a package name but not its complete revision?
case.answer: Request the missing evidence; do not treat an incomplete observation as a clean assessment.

case.title: Decide applicability
case.input: The source revision, asset observation and supported native-version rules.
case.action: Apply deterministic vendor-aware comparisons and configuration conditions. Follow the unknown branch: request the exact missing field, obtain authorized fresh evidence and rerun D09. Continue the repair path only if affected is established.
case.output: In this teaching case, unknown until the required missing evidence arrives; affected only if the qualified rules then establish it.
case.because: Unknown and not_affected must stay distinct. The assistant cannot fill a missing configuration fact.
case.question: Could semantic similarity between the advisory and OS name establish the verdict?
case.answer: No. It can propose a candidate; D09 needs version/configuration semantics and traceable evidence.

case.title: Choose the action to discuss first
case.owner: Mahrous; Omar displays the policy output
case.input: For this branch, targeted collection has supplied the missing field and D09 has established affected. Use that qualified finding, dated threat signals and declared organization context; unresolved cases remain outside the confirmed repair path.
case.action: Produce explained policy bands and compatible grouped remediation actions.
case.output: A reasoned action queue with asset/CVE drill-down and separate unknown, no-patch and constrained cases.
case.because: Ten CVEs are not necessarily ten different repair actions. Grouping must respect compatibility and policy.
case.question: Why not simply choose the largest CVSS score?
case.answer: Severity is one input. Exploitation evidence, exposure, criticality, freshness and fix constraints have different meanings.

case.title: Explain the evidence
case.owner: Hams leads behavior/retrieval; Omar integrates the API
case.input: An authorized question, current structured assessment and permitted source/policy text.
case.action: Use read-only tools and retrieval, then return citations, limits and precise missing-evidence requests.
case.output: An explanation or constrained draft, never a patch approval or command.
case.because: The model adds an understandable explanation without owning the security verdict.
case.question: Where is live asset state obtained: model memory, RAG text or authorized tools?
case.answer: Current structured facts come from authorized tools; retrieval supplies governed explanatory evidence.

case.title: Bind a plan to approval
case.owner: Mahrous defines policy; Omar implements platform states
case.input: Exact targets, validated fix evidence, current revisions, permitted window and recovery constraints.
case.action: Build the immutable plan and require a scoped, expiring approval checked again before dispatch.
case.output: An approved plan only when every required policy condition holds.
case.because: Changing targets, evidence or the plan can invalidate an earlier approval.
case.question: Can a persuasive assistant recommendation authorize the runner?
case.answer: No. C10 policy and P12 platform states enforce the separate approval boundary.

case.title: Run the approved pilot
case.input: A typed approved job, authenticated runner and qualified disposable lab target.
case.action: Recheck identity/preflight and use the selected native-update adapter within its allowlist.
case.output: Execution evidence and explicit success, failure, reboot-pending or uncertain outcome.
case.because: The web API and LLM must not acquire arbitrary shell authority.
case.question: The connection is lost after mutation starts. Retry immediately?
case.answer: No. Reconcile the target first; transport retry does not establish whether the update already happened.

case.title: Verify the actual result
case.owner: Mahrous; Shams supports independent collection and Amr recovery
case.input: Fresh independent inventory, running/service evidence and execution history.
case.action: Reassess and check the adapter-specific service state; rehearse recovery when necessary.
case.output: Verified closure, remaining exposure or a linked reopened episode with history preserved.
case.because: A successful command is not the same as a fixed and healthy system.
case.question: The finding returns later. Have we proved human error?
case.answer: No. Separate repeated observation, changed advisory evidence and recurrence after verified closure. A cause needs supporting evidence.

case.title: Follow the evidence across the platform
case.owner: Omar; Mahrous defines the security event meaning
case.input: Versioned source, observation, assessment, plan and execution event identities.
case.action: Keep traceable history, update derived answers on revisions and qualify deployment separately from application behavior.
case.output: Reproducible evidence links; qualified SIEM decoding/correlation when that integration passes its gate.
case.because: A screenshot of a page or a delivered event is not proof that every downstream interpretation worked.
case.question: Does this walkthrough claim that the product or these experiments are implemented?
case.answer: No. This is a static teaching case explaining the retained plan and its validation requirements.

people.name: Amr
people.role: Vulnerability intelligence, vendor evidence and tool trust
people.ar: تخلّي المعلومة موثوقة ومفهومة قبل ما نستخدمها.

people.tools: Python/HTTP, raw JSON and versioned schemas; official CVE/vendor/NVD adapters. Exact source quotas, rights and profile coverage remain execution checks.
people.connect: D02 feeds P02/A06. D05 and D14 support applicability and remediation. D17 is conditional FortiOS qualification; D18 governs permitted tool/data use.
people.avoid: Calling public availability permission to redistribute, or calling a fixed-version floor a complete upgrade path.

people.name: Shams
people.ar: تجمع بيانات الجهاز الفعلية وتحافظ على هوية الدليل وتاريخه.
people.understand: Discovery versus authenticated inventory; stable host identity; native package evidence; stale, incomplete and failed collection.
people.tools: Scoped Nmap, authenticated SSH/native inventory, qualified Windows inventory and offline imports. Amr supplies the lab and retains patch execution.
people.connect: Asset contracts and collectors feed identity/history/quality; C20/C21 reuse Omar’s job boundary, D08/D09/D13 retain matching/reassessment, Amr retains source data and patch/recovery, and C22 tests the asset-only contribution.
people.avoid: Treating an unreachable or stale asset as a clean successful inventory.

people.name: Mahrous
people.ar: يحوّل الدليل لقرار مبرَّر، من غير ما يخمّن الناقص.
people.understand: Product identity, native version comparisons, unknown states, policy reason codes, approval binding and independent verification.
people.tools: Deterministic rules, vendor-native version comparators and reviewed fixtures. KEV/EPSS/CVSS retain their different meanings; no fabricated risk probability.
people.connect: C03 joins source/asset contracts in P02. D09 is the one applicability engine reused by C08. D12 feeds P10; C10 feeds P12; C13 establishes verified closure.
people.avoid: Reimplementing matching in C08 or letting an AI answer approve a change.

people.name: Hams
people.ar: تختبر قيمة الذكاء الاصطناعي وتخلّي الرحلة مفهومة للمستخدم.
people.understand: Labels and splits; baseline versus stronger model; retrieval versus live tools; citation/evaluation; user flows and uncertainty states.
people.tools: TF-IDF/linear CPU baseline; exact and lexical retrieval before optional dense search/reranking. Local model/runtime selected through A09. UX design tool is not selected by this study guide.
people.connect: A06 uses D02 source metadata. A07/A09 inform P11/A10; Omar owns API integration. UX02 provides the reviewed design for Omar’s P05; optional models wait for evidence and capacity.
people.avoid: Calling SecBERT a generative assistant, adding current CVEs through routine retraining, or taking UI implementation ownership away from Omar.

people.name: Omar
people.ar: يربط الأجزاء بنفس المعاني ويجهّز تشغيلها واستعادتها.
people.understand: Shared contracts, revisions, object permissions, durable jobs, gateway boundaries and connected/disconnected deployment.
people.tools: FastAPI conditional default; React/TypeScript/Vite candidate for the product; PostgreSQL/JSONB core; conditional broker/vector choices. Linux Compose hosting is qualified on measured hardware. This planning site remains buildless.
people.connect: P02 integrates C03/D02; P05 implements Hams’s UX02; P10 consumes D12. P11/A10 share one gateway; P14 and P17 cover separate hosting qualifications.
people.avoid: A second matching or approval engine in the frontend, public database/model/runner ports, or assuming a local LLM makes the whole system offline.

Keep their meanings distinct; none supplies all organization context.
