questions: Why is the AI not simply checking whether an OS has a CVE?

The OS name generates possible matches, but D09 needs exact vendor/product, package revision and relevant configuration evidence. Retrieval helps explain evidence; it cannot substitute for the qualified version rules.
ADR04
If the CVEs are in RAG, why do we also need PostgreSQL?

We need explicit records, relationships, revisions, permissions and current state. Source/policy text may be indexed for retrieval, while the database and authorized tools answer current structured questions.
ADR11
Do new CVEs require training the LLM again?

No routine retraining or fine-tuning is planned. The intelligence pipeline ingests evidence and refreshes retrieval/assessments. A05 may compare frozen encoders plus a classifier. Any future fine-tuning needs the separate OQ01 review. D16 measures freshness.
ADR23
What makes the top ten useful?

The chosen primary unit is up to ten compatible remediation actions, not ten repeated CVE rows. The queue retains reasons, asset/finding drill-down and constrained/unknown cases. Its benefit remains a measured hypothesis, not a proven superiority claim.
ADR24
Can we scan every non-Windows device?

No. Authorization, reachability, credentials, protocol support, identity/version semantics and device safety each constrain capability. The narrow profile uses Ubuntu lab execution and conditional FortiOS evidence imports/recommendations. Direct OT probing is excluded.
ADR21
Does on-prem mean we must buy an expensive server now?

Actual available hardware and cost are unknown until P01/A09 measurement. The plan prepares local-capable contracts and storage now, qualifies connected hosting in P14, and separately qualifies disconnected bundles in P17.
ADR22
Is a local LLM enough to call the system offline?
No. Embeddings, models/tokenizers, identity, DNS/certificate trust, telemetry, feeds and package content can still require network access. P17 tests the enabled profile with public egress blocked.
ADR22
Who owns UI/UX, and who writes the UI?
Hams leads user research, flows, state design and usability. Omar implements the frontend. UX02 is the reviewed design input to P05; the same fields and uncertainty states must make sense in both.
UX01
UX02
UX03
ADR10
Why not just use the latest available firmware?

A vendor fixed-version floor does not establish model compatibility, allowed train, intermediate upgrade steps, support entitlement or recovery. D14/D17 retain those constraints; automatic FortiOS firmware execution is not in the release.
ADR21
How are repeated problems handled without blaming people?

Separate repeated observations from reopening after verified closure and source changes. A cause remains a hypothesis until reviewed evidence supports it. The meeting’s 90%-people statement is not a verified statistic.
ADR24
Are the New/Updated markers proof that experiments or tasks are complete?
No. They identify edits to the plan. Source-review dates, proposed validation gates and the date of explanatory content are separate. This edition adds no live task reporting or completion dashboard.
ADR20
Will the website now sync our ClickUp workspace?

No. The personal study features do not need task synchronization. No ClickUp connection, workspace access or task write is introduced. The existing prepared CSV remains a separate artifact; opening a workspace link is navigation, not live synchronization.
ADR08
talk: Teams face many advisories but need to know which installed assets are actually affected and which compatible repair matters first. We focus on supported industrial IT, not a universal OT scanner.
Amr makes advisory/source assertions traceable. Shams collects authorized asset facts. Mahrous joins both through vendor-aware rules with an explicit unknown state.
Policy adds threat and organization context. The queue groups compatible actions and explains reasons; no invented compromise probability is presented.
Hams defines and evaluates classification, retrieval and grounded explanations. Current facts remain in typed tools; Omar integrates the shared gateway and implements Hams’s UX design.
Approval is bound to the exact plan. Amr executes a qualified lab pilot through an isolated runner. Independent evidence and health checks establish closure.

Omar connects the contracts, permissions, durable jobs and hosting. Connected on-prem and disconnected delivery have separate proof gates. This describes our plan; experiments and customer fit are not claimed complete.

overview.meaning: The product workflow, the current implementation slice and links to each person’s full task scope.
overview.when: You need to explain what AegisLoop does, distinguish the whole product from this week’s prototype, or open a team workspace.
overview.example: See evidence → applicability → prioritization → approved remediation → verification, then open the 1/5 November prototype plan.
overview.caution: Static project explanation. No team completion or delivery reporting is inferred.

study.meaning: Your personal route through concepts, examples, people and discussion questions.
study.when: When you understand an individual term but cannot explain how it connects to the rest of AegisLoop.
study.example: Compare an asset observation, an applicability verdict and an assistant explanation using the same teaching case.
study.caution: Nothing here records team progress or a personal learning score.

revision.meaning: The agreed boundaries and the reasons recent scope, AI, UX and on-prem details changed.
revision.when: When someone asks whether FortiOS firmware execution, generic OT scanning or external inference belongs in this release.
revision.example: Compare the supported-profile matrix with Omar’s P14 connected-hosting plan and P17 disconnected qualification.
revision.caution: New/Updated is a plan-edit label. Exact profiles, hardware and customer fit still have explicit validation gates.

system.meaning: How source knowledge, asset evidence, rules, assistant and runner are connected.
system.when: When you need to explain who produces a security verdict or why chat cannot directly patch a device.
system.example: Select Assess applicability, then Version-bound approval and Isolated execution; notice their different owners and inputs.
system.caution: Arrows show planned evidence/data flow, not observed production traffic.

work.meaning: The complete execution plan with visible search, filters, delivery labels and separate owned/supporting task groups.
work.when: You want to find a task, review all of someone’s work, or filter the plan to a prototype checkpoint.
work.example: Open Hams for all her tasks. From her 5 November prototype page, Same tasks in Execution opens that delivery only; All Hams tasks restores the complete scope.
work.caution: Prerequisites describe the plan. No local completion or actual blocked status is shown.

delivery.meaning: The planned implementation order, interfaces and possible parallel branches.
delivery.when: When you want to understand why P05 follows UX02 or how different people can prepare compatible fixtures.
delivery.example: Inspect P05: P02 supplies the contract and UX02 the reviewed design. A shell can be explored earlier; completed flows need the design input.
delivery.caution: This is dependency logic, not a live schedule. Core-chain flags are not a duration-calculated critical path.

team.meaning: Each person’s engineering domain, owned guides and supporting connections.
team.when: When preparing to explain the work of a teammate or identify whose technical judgment a question needs.
team.example: Amr owns vulnerability/advisory data; Shams owns asset inventory. Amr retains lab/patch execution; Hams owns UX design and Omar implements the UI.
team.caution: Assignments are the plan; this page does not say who has delivered anything.

decisions.meaning: Decision Log means why a technical approach was recommended and what evidence could change it.
decisions.when: When you ask why deterministic rules, why PostgreSQL, or why on-prem is staged instead of a fallback.
decisions.example: ADR04 explains applicability rules; ADR11 separates structured truth and retrieval; ADR22 explains the on-prem stages.
decisions.caution: Original research and later clarifications are retained. A recommendation is not a completed experiment.

risks.meaning: Risk Radar collects possible failure modes, early clues and response options.
risks.when: When a design choice looks easy but you want to understand what could invalidate it.
risks.example: R23: incompatible Hams/Mahrous fields. R24: hidden online dependencies. R26: UX and AI competing for Hams’s capacity.
risks.caution: 27 qualitative planned risks are retained; additions R23–R27 are visible. None is claimed observed or mitigated by a change badge.

validation.meaning: The experiments and expected evidence that could support a project claim.
validation.when: When you need to understand what detection quality, retrieval quality or a successful patch demonstration actually means.
validation.example: D15 requires declared cases/denominators; A07 separates retrieval evidence; C13 requires fresh inventory and health checks.
validation.caution: These are protocols and targets. No accuracy, pass result or experiment completion is asserted.

evidence.meaning: The retained technical reasoning and primary-source starting points behind the plan.
evidence.when: When an explanation depends on a vendor rule, a license, an API limit or a tool capability that you want to verify.
evidence.example: Use D17’s source links to separate Fortinet affected/fixed assertions from the reviewed full upgrade path.
evidence.caution: Each source retains its own review date. A newer page edit does not mean every source was reverified that day.

open.meaning: Unresolved discussion and research questions, kept separate from adopted directions and approved ADRs.
open.when: A meeting phrase is ambiguous, evidence is missing, or you need to see what still needs a decision.
open.example: Open OQ01 to see what a future fine-tuning proposal must establish; OQ02 covers product interaction design.
open.caution: These are static planning questions, not task completion states. They do not add dependency edges or change primary owners.

reference.meaning: Optional technical reference for questions that go beyond this week’s instructions.
reference.when: You need architecture, research evidence, a decision rationale or the full risk/test register.
reference.example: Open a package’s tests and risks first; use the complete reference only if that context is not enough.
reference.caution: The original deep links and research remain available. Reference content does not report actual work completion.

workflow.meaning: Project stages, or the exact inputs and downstream consumers of one task.
workflow.when: You need to see who produces your inputs and who uses your result.
workflow.example: D09 uses Amr’s vendor data and Shams’s asset evidence; C08 connects its result to the platform.
workflow.caution: These are planned relationships, not completion or lateness reports.

outputs.meaning: A task output is the result its owner delivers. It becomes an input to downstream tasks.
outputs.when: You need to know what to deliver, or need a labelled reference while developing an upstream boundary.
outputs.example: Shams’s C05 reference represents asset observations. Mahrous uses that shape to develop D09.
outputs.caution: Research packs are separate from handoff packets. Imported deliveries still need content and acceptance review, and are browser-local.
outputs.nextLabel: Open the output and input owners

D01.question: What does CVE.org provide versus NVD enrichment?
D01.method: Python collector prototype, official CVE records plus independent NVD enrichment, raw JSON and a draft schema. This is a local-file spike; D02 owns the validated shared schema, and D03 owns the production intake pipeline.

D02.question: Which fields are required, nullable or provider-specific in the D01 samples?
D02.method: Versioned JSON Schema and immutable source revisions; relational integration in P03 follows P02. Draft prototypes remain file-based until the persistence contract is agreed.
D02.misread: Alias conflation creates wrong findings and duplicate metrics.

D03.question: Which official snapshot and revision mechanism will the selected CVE adapter use?
D03.method: Official CVEListV5 baseline plus incremental changes, checksums, idempotent upserts and durable checkpoints. Choose exact download mechanics from D01 evidence; no scraping dependency.
D03.misread: Git history gaps or schema changes silently skip records.

D04.question: Which fields and schema revisions are exposed by the current endpoint?
D04.method: Independent NVD adapter with conservative pacing, backoff and provenance. Current numeric NVD quotas remain RESEARCH REQUIRED until primary documentation is available; they are not hard-coded from memory.
D04.misread: Assuming all NVD records are enriched delays or loses detection.

D05.question: How do Ubuntu CVE, USN and LSN records differ?
D05.method: Official Ubuntu OSV JSON first, selected OVAL cross-check. Preserve distro/architecture/source-package identity; selected release and data-usage terms need execution-time validation.

D06.question: How do MSRC product trees, build identities and superseding updates relate?
D06.method: Microsoft advisory data plus endpoint servicing evidence; Red Hat CSAF/VEX. New OVAL-only RHEL investment is not the chosen default; full Windows execution stays in C14.
D06.misread: Windows servicing and product identity consume more effort than anticipated.

D07.question: Which selected ecosystems and purl forms are in scope?
D07.method: OSV query/cache for chosen ecosystems and native advisory IDs. A public API is not universal vulnerability coverage or blanket permission to redistribute all upstream content.
D07.misread: OSV has no documented current quota but bulk queries can still fail or change policy.

D08.question: Which inventory fields identify vendor, distro, package ecosystem, product branch and architecture?
D08.method: Internal asset IDs plus typed vendor/CPE/purl identities. Fuzzy matches can propose candidates; they cannot establish an affected verdict.
D08.misread: Banner strings are stale, masked or vendor-customized.

D09.question: Which native version comparator matches each supported ecosystem?
D09.method: Deterministic vendor-aware rules, source revisions and explicit reason codes. Reuse this engine in C08; neither embeddings nor the LLM decides version applicability.
D09.misread: Naive semver or lexical order misclassifies OS packages.

D10.question: Which supported SBOM/VEX formats are actually available from the test product?
D10.method: Selected CycloneDX/CSAF/VEX input profiles behind a validated adapter. Do not implement every standard at once; exact supported versions remain Needs Validation.
D10.misread: Untrusted VEX suppresses a genuine finding.

D11.question: Which KEV fields and update timestamps should be retained?
D11.method: Official KEV data plus daily bulk EPSS where appropriate; separate signals, bounded API access and dated provenance. FIRST quotas and API behavior follow the retained source register.
D11.misread: EPSS forecast is mislabeled asset-specific probability.

D12.question: Which exposure and business criticality values can the lab actually provide?
D12.method: Rule-based bands retaining CVSS, KEV, EPSS and local context separately. Policy weights and deadlines are project decisions requiring review; no arbitrary score is marketed as calibrated risk.
D12.misread: Unvalidated weights look scientific but mislead.

D13.question: Which changed fields affect applicability, priority, patch options or only display text?
D13.method: Versioned change events, idempotent consumers and current-result views. NVD enrichment is optional and must not block CVE/vendor reassessment; A14 adds AI-specific operations on this path.
D13.misread: Event storms exhaust resources after bulk upstream changes.

D14.question: Where does each vendor publish fixed versions and alternative mitigations?
D14.method: Vendor-authoritative remediation assertions; C09 validates their execution readiness. Newest release is not automatically the compatible target, and missing fixed versions must not be invented.
D14.misread: A real fix is unavailable to this entitlement or platform.

D15.question: Who labels each case independently of the matching code?
D15.method: Frozen source/observation revisions and independent labels, not another scanner treated as ground truth. The proposal detection target applies only to declared known vulnerabilities in the controlled lab.
D15.misread: Easy-only dataset inflates results and academic value collapses.

D16.question: Which timestamps measure publication, first observed, normalized, indexed and reassessed?
D16.method: Keep the proposal 24-hour target; polling and recovery scheduling are configurable. Unknown public disclosure times and incomplete upstream data remain visible limitations.
D16.misread: Publication timestamps are revised/backdated, distorting freshness metrics.

C01.question: Which exact networks and devices does the team control?
C01.method: Allowlisted scopes, resolved-address revalidation, device-specific profiles and bounded operations. This defines lab authorization, not permission to scan an external organization.
C01.misread: IP reuse or hostname resolution changes

C02.question: Which available hardware supports the chosen VM and network layout?
C02.method: Isolated VM/network with pinned images and known package fixtures. Exact hypervisor and target release remain Needs Validation against available hardware; serialized VMs are an allowed fallback.

C03.question: Which fields identify an enrolled host beyond IP?
C03.method: Versioned JSON observation schema coordinated with P02; enrollment identity and evidence references are explicit. This is the domain specification, not a second platform schema engine.

C04.question: Which conservative Nmap profile fits each approved device class?
C04.method: Separately installed Nmap with fixed argument arrays, exclusions, time and concurrency limits. No blanket aggressive script profile; product redistribution is a separate licensing gate.

C05.question: Which native output exposes distro release, architecture and binary/source package identity?
C05.method: Authenticated SSH with host-key verification and structured native inventory. Choose parser/dependency versions in the lab spike; avoid broad shell/environment dumps.
C05.misread: permission gaps or command parsing drift

C06.question: Does osquery or existing Wazuh Syscollector expose the required build, package and update fields?
C06.method: Experimental Decision: compare osquery and Wazuh, prefer existing deployment where justified, then implement one primary adapter. A recorded export is not live Windows validation.

C07.question: Which exact model, firmware train and hardware revision identify the test appliance?
C07.method: Validated JSON/vendor-export adapter with bounded uploads and explicit manual/import labels. General OT active scanning and universal firmware updating remain out of scope.

C08.question: Does the D09 contract carry source revision, observation ID, reason codes and missing evidence?
C08.method: Reuse D09 as the only matching engine. C08 owns integration and evidence review, while P06 displays the result; no parallel matching implementation is needed.

C09.question: Is the documented fix actually available from the target's configured repository?
C09.method: Reuse the versioned D14 catalog; add applicability, availability and execution precondition checks. A download URL or AI recommendation is not approval.

C10.question: Who may propose, approve and dispatch in the four-role policy?
C10.method: Immutable version/hash-bound plans with explicit scope and permission checks, coordinated with P12. Human approval is checked again immediately before mutation.

C11.question: Which native package or Ansible operation can enforce exact versions and trusted repositories?
C11.method: Isolated allowlisted runner using native package mechanisms, with Ansible as the first adapter candidate. No arbitrary shell from the user or assistant; exact runner choice is validated in the lab.

C12.question: How is reboot need detected for each supported adapter?
C12.method: Durable attempt records, bounded reconnect and explicit reboot_pending/outcome_unknown states. Transport retry is not permission to repeat a non-idempotent update.

C13.question: Which installed versus running version checks matter for the chosen update?
C13.method: Independent collection and deterministic reassessment plus adapter-specific service checks. No universal rollback claim; recovery must be rehearsed for the selected lab target.
C13.misread: snapshot loses data or package downgrade unsupported

C14.question: Which configured update service supplies applicable updates on the licensed test build?
C14.method: Experimental Decision: native Windows servicing through the selected supported adapter, including ansible.windows.win_updates candidate. Jobs may run for hours; C06 inventory alone does not prove patch capability.

C15.question: Which Wazuh agent/localfile and JSON decoder configuration is deployed in the lab?
C15.method: P13 outbox delivers JSON lines to the supported Wazuh collection route. The management REST API is not assumed to be a generic event ingestion endpoint.

C16.question: Which fixtures and supported profiles form the fixed denominator?
C16.method: Controlled-lab metrics and reproducible evidence; optional scanner comparisons are secondary, not ground truth. Repeat the relevant subset at each discussion and freeze final results at G4.

A01.question: Which category and impact labels can overlap?
A01.method: Multilabel category/impact taxonomy with explicit unknowns; official CVSS remains primary. Labels are project definitions, not an official universal CVE taxonomy.

A02.question: Which source revisions and fields are allowed in each AI task?
A02.method: Versioned JSONL and dataset manifests from preserved evidence, with human-reviewed labels. User feedback and LLM-generated labels are not automatic ground truth.
A02.misread: Dataset revisions silently change reported scores.

A03.question: Which HTML/Unicode normalization preserves negation, IDs and version strings?
A03.method: Group-aware chronological split with a locked final holdout; explicit severity leakage controls. TimeSeriesSplit alone does not solve advisory alias leakage.
A03.misread: Pretrained-model knowledge of older CVEs remains possible.

A04.question: Which keyword and TF-IDF baselines answer the defined tasks?
A04.method: Word/character TF-IDF with OneVsRest logistic regression or linear SVM candidates. Choose thresholds on validation only; no fixed final F1 promise before label audit.
A04.misread: Small labels or imbalance makes overall accuracy misleading.

A05.question: Which error categories are label problems rather than model failures?
A05.method: Review disagreements and compare frozen encoder features plus a classifier against the baseline. Fine-tuning is excluded from current implementation; OQ01 holds the future capability review.
A05.misread: A stronger classifier experiment does not authorize fine-tuning now. Future model adaptation needs an explicit business, data, resource and evaluation case.

A06.question: Which advisory sections should be kept together to avoid mixing product rows?
A06.method: Structured chunks and metadata in the existing PostgreSQL design; embeddings are derived. Corpus fixtures allow development before the full live intake is ready.
A06.misread: Chunk boundaries mix fixed versions across products.

A07.question: Does lexical-only search already answer exact IDs and product questions?
A07.method: Exact IDs plus PostgreSQL text search, with pgvector dense retrieval only if measured useful. E5-small and BGE-M3 are candidates; use documented prefixes and model revisions.
A07.misread: Embedding similarity misses precise identifiers or confuses version strings.

A08.question: Are missed answers caused by candidate absence or poor ranking?
A08.method: Experimental Decision, optional G3 enhancement. Do not add a new inference dependency unless its measured gain exceeds the added cost.
A08.misread: Extra inference causes timeouts with little gain.

A09.question: Can the exact model revision, runtime and quantization support the required chat/tool schema?
A09.method: Needs Validation: researched Qwen3.5-4B/Qwen3 Instruct/Gemma3 shortlist. Local serving and exact runtime remain experimental; hosted services need a separate budget/privacy gate.
A09.misread: Unknown hardware cannot sustain even a small model.

A10.question: Which allowed intents map to get_asset_summary, explain_applicability and advisory retrieval?
A10.method: One shared A10/P11 gateway: Hams owns behavior/retrieval, Omar owns API and authorization. Read-only tools; drafting is separate from approval or execution.
A10.misread: Schema-valid text can still contain false claims.

A11.question: Which missing fields would change a specific unknown verdict?
A11.method: Use deterministic assessment gaps and D14/C10 facts through bounded tools. The LLM phrases supported options; it does not invent a patch plan or decide applicability.
A11.misread: LLM omits prerequisite/reboot or implies mitigation fixes vulnerability.

A12.question: Which malicious instructions can enter through advisory text or tool outputs?
A12.method: Authorization and allowlisted tools are enforced by code; prompts and RAG are not security boundaries. No credentials enter the model context.
A12.misread: Prompt defenses may fail despite good average results.

A13.question: Which question categories cover the declared user tasks and failure cases?
A13.method: Human-reviewed source-grounded questions, with LLM judging only as optional assistance. Pilot sample sizes are planning targets, not evidence of statistical sufficiency.

A14.question: Which evidence, prompt, model and user-scope fields belong in cache keys?
A14.method: Reuse D13 change events and P09 health, adding AI-specific cache/model metadata. No duplicate scheduler and no automatic self-training from votes.
A14.misread: Re-embedding migration mixes incompatible vector spaces.

A15.question: Do change-aware explanations reduce time-to-correct-decision versus the frozen baseline?
A15.method: Evaluate narrow hypotheses: revision-aware decisions, targeted evidence requests and constrained remediation. Tenable already documents agents/approvals/workflows; no blanket superiority claim.
A15.misread: Adding more features is mistaken for scientific novelty.

A16.question: Which licenses and hashes must accompany the selected model and dataset?
A16.method: Versioned experiment manifests, source attribution, deterministic seeds where applicable and honest limits. No unvalidated candidate is presented as the final chosen model.
A16.misread: Only one member understands model internals.

P01.question: Which backend/frontend frameworks can Omar actually build and maintain today?
P01.method: FastAPI conditional default with Django/NestJS alternatives already researched. Needs Validation against skills and authentication integration; preserve contracts if the framework changes.

P02.question: Do C03 and D02 samples agree on IDs, timestamps, revisions and unknown states?
P02.method: OpenAPI/JSON Schema with versioned fixtures. C03/D02 provide domain definitions; P02 integrates them rather than inventing competing schemas.
P02.misread: Teams silently use different meanings for version/status

P03.question: Which entities need relational keys versus flexible JSONB?
P03.method: PostgreSQL relational core plus JSONB; SQLAlchemy/Alembic if FastAPI wins. ORM choice follows P01; retrieval is a separate derived concern.
P03.misread: JSON blobs obscure identity and transitions

P04.question: Which maintained auth/session component fits the chosen framework?
P04.method: Revocable cookie sessions with server-side scope checks, plus separate scoped runner credentials. Exact component Needs Validation; Keycloak/OIDC remains the researched fallback.
P04.misread: UI hides buttons but API still permits action

P05.question: Which screens are required for the first real slice?
P05.method: React/TypeScript/Vite candidate for the product dashboard, subject to P01. This planning website stays buildless; do not confuse its UI implementation with the product stack.

P06.question: Which authorized observation and advisory are suitable for the first slice?
P06.method: Shared contracts and D09/C08 engine through the existing API. A mock-only interface is preparation, not proof of the real integration gate.

P07.question: Can Celery/RabbitMQ fit the actual laptop and learning budget?
P07.method: PostgreSQL ledger/outbox with conditional Celery/RabbitMQ broker spike. A bounded serial durable worker is the fallback; in-process request background tasks are not the reliability mechanism.
P07.misread: Retry executes patch twice or broker exhausts laptop

P08.question: How is runner enrollment authenticated and revoked?
P08.method: Authenticated typed job channel, allowlisted adapters and secret references. No Docker socket or arbitrary shell authority in the web API; exact enrollment transport is validated before use.
P08.misread: Compromised API becomes privileged remote shell

P09.question: Which source-health fields distinguish last attempt from last success?
P09.method: P03/P07 state plus D03 ingestion metadata; no second ingestion scheduler. D13 and A14 consume the same current source revision facts.
P09.misread: Dashboard looks healthy while feeds stalled

P10.question: Which assessment and priority fields are authoritative versus predicted?
P10.method: Consume D09/D12 outputs and history through server-side authorization. The UI does not recalculate version applicability or turn unknown into a clean result.
P10.misread: Severity presented as proven exploitation probability

P11.question: How is current user scope applied before retrieval and every tool call?
P11.method: Single gateway shared with A10; Omar owns API/auth integration and Hams owns retrieval/answer behavior. Exact LLM choice follows A09 rather than being embedded in UI code.
P11.misread: Assistant bypasses API scopes or sends secrets upstream

P12.question: Which transitions are allowed before/after approval and mutation?
P12.method: C10 policy and P08 runner boundary, version-bound plans and durable attempts. Reuse native patch adapters; do not implement a second approval engine in the frontend.

P13.question: Which event schema and correlation IDs does the consumer need?
P13.method: Transactional PostgreSQL outbox and supported JSON-lines Wazuh route. At-least-once delivery is explicit; duplicate delivery must not create duplicate business findings.
P13.misread: HTTP success mistaken for SIEM correlation

P14.question: Which services can share a host and which need separate profiles?
P14.method: Linux Compose profiles and private filesystem evidence adapter initially. Exact versions/TLS setup need validation; proposed RPO/RTO are test targets, not guarantees. No new legacy MinIO dependency. Hosting detail: retain the measured Linux/Compose deployment. Host/provider, domain, TLS proxy/issuer, sizes and availability targets are Needs Validation; this plan does not provision or purchase infrastructure.

P15.question: Which versioned ASVS controls apply to the actual product scope?
P15.method: Use existing module tests plus cross-boundary scenarios and selected ASVS/SSDF guidance. This is release evidence, not a claim of security certification or a complete penetration test.
P15.misread: Happy-path demo hides unsafe edge cases

P16.question: Which declared asset/CVE/query volumes represent the final benchmark?
P16.method: Measure pagination, indexes and concurrency before adding infrastructure. Preserve pinned dependencies, source/model licenses and clean restore; no enterprise-scale claim from the student lab.
P16.misread: Unbounded scope prevents reliable final demo

UX01.question: Who is the first user: analyst, approver or administrator, and what must each decide?
UX01.method: Low-fidelity user flows and task scenarios; design tool remains the team choice. Hams leads research/design; Omar implements.
UX01.misread: UI research competes with Hams model experiments.

UX02.question: Which summary fields make the top ten actions understandable without hiding affected assets?
UX02.method: Contract-driven prototype, progressive disclosure and evidence-first wording. Hams owns design; P05 remains Omar-owned implementation.
UX02.misread: Prototype assumes API fields that do not exist.

UX03.question: Which tasks can reviewers complete correctly without coaching?
UX03.method: Task-based usability study; no invented participant count or target success percentage. Hams leads; Omar implements corrections.
UX03.misread: Small samples are overclaimed as market validation.

D17.question: Can the public PSIRT/RSS and per-advisory CSAF mechanism be fetched reproducibly under current terms?
D17.method: Vendor assertions and typed revision links; public RSS is discovery, not proof that all revisions are captured. This profile is conditional and does not block the Ubuntu core.
D17.misread: Public advisory retrieval changes or is blocked.

D18.question: Which exact artifact/version/license and owner apply to each enabled dependency?
D18.method: Evidence-based trust/rights register with release-specific scope; legal or procurement confirmation remains required where the terms are unclear.
D18.misread: Software license is mistaken for rights to all ingested content.

P17.question: Which exact CPU/GPU architecture, RAM, disk and container runtime pass the measured profile?
P17.method: Extend retained Compose deployment and local PostgreSQL/evidence paths; no Kubernetes requirement. Offline qualification is a planned product milestone, not a claim that the current planning website runs the product.
P17.misread: Runtime startup pulls a tokenizer, font, image, identity or telemetry dependency.

A17.question: Does AI or hybrid ranking improve the same reviewed action queue?
A17.method: RESEARCH REQUIRED: reuse D12 rules and A02/A03 data. First build a Python offline comparison harness; choose one low-resource AI candidate after evidence review, then test rules-first hybrid constrained ordering. No fine-tuning in current execution. LLM text is not an authoritative risk probability.
A17.misread: Hams owns the capability, not every domain implementation. An AI experiment may correctly recommend keeping the rule baseline.

C17.question: Which identity signals survive IP changes, re-enrollment and host cloning, and which conflicts must block an automatic association?
C17.method: Deferred multi-source identity after demonstrated conflicts and delivered persistence/auth.
C17.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

C18.question: Which package/service/OS changes are comparable across collector versions and incomplete snapshots?
C18.method: Small pure snapshot diff on a stable enrolled host; no mandatory full reconciliation.
C18.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

C19.question: Which freshness windows and mandatory fields are defensible for each supported asset/collection profile?
C19.method: Pure field-quality evaluator from a snapshot and explicit time; no mandatory delta history.
C19.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

C20.question: Which approved probe supplies each asset field, and which fields cannot be collected in the current scope?
C20.method: Optional measured evidence-gap collection after the core protocol/baselines.
C20.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

C21.question: Which batch/concurrency/time/traffic limits protect the chosen authorized lab/device classes?
C21.method: Deferred asset batching through the existing ledger after a measured load need.
C21.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

C22.question: Which independently reviewed asset facts and change sequences exercise false merges, missed changes, stale evidence and partial collection?
C22.method: Design the independent protocol early, evaluate the core first, then add qualified experiments.
C22.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

C23.question: Which package/service/host relationships can the existing authorized collectors actually substantiate?
C23.method: Optional narrow observed service context; no inferred business graph.
C23.misread: Treating optional breadth or synthetic expected cases as delivered project value.

openQuestions.purpose: Keep unresolved questions visible without presenting meeting notes as approved architecture, live blockers or task progress. Discussion stewards coordinate answers; primary package ownership and dependencies are unchanged.
directions: An integrated vulnerability-to-remediation platform: evidence collection, applicability, categorization, policy-aware prioritization, reviewed remediation, controlled execution and verification. Chat is an assisting interaction within the platform.

No fine-tuning in the current implementation. Retain retrieval, reviewed organization context, current structured facts, baseline classification and evaluation. Training a baseline classifier is distinct from fine-tuning pretrained weights.

Build toward a sustainable startup, with staged on-prem capability. Revisit expensive capabilities when evidence, customer requirements and business value justify their full delivery and maintenance costs.
Not prohibited forever and not scheduled now. OQ01 records the decision gates and preparation needed before any future experiment. Company size alone does not decide suitability.

items.title: When would fine-tuning earn its cost?
items.context: Deferred capability, not current execution. Distinguish classifier adaptation from generative-model adaptation.
questions: Which repeated failure remains after fixing labels, retrieval, prompts and tools?
What exact task, eligible model and legally usable reviewed dataset would be needed?
How would identical held-out evaluations prove added value, safety and absence of leakage?
What RAM/GPU, training time, total cost, model-serving capacity and specialist skills are required?
How would we version data/weights, reproduce runs, evaluate regressions, deploy, roll back and maintain a tuned model on-prem?
Could a smaller model, frozen encoder or improved workflow meet the same requirement more economically?
items.closeWith: A scoped proposal comparing alternatives and measured baseline failures; data/rights review; resource estimate; reproducible experiment and release/rollback/evaluation plan. No training until the proposal is accepted.
items.timing: Future capability review only; no new blocker for the current release.

items.title: Which product views best support each user action?
items.context: Platform identity is settled. The balance of action queues, asset/evidence pages, approvals and conversational assistance still needs user validation.
questions: Which role needs an asset view, priority queue, evidence drill-down, approval screen or chat at each step?
Can a user identify a priority, inspect its reason, review a plan and verify the result without relying on a conversation transcript?
Where does a cited conversational interaction reduce effort compared with structured controls?
items.closeWith: A reviewed end-to-end UX prototype and usability findings; Hams leads research/design and Omar implements the accepted states. No assumption that the product is a standalone chatbot.
items.timing: Resolve interaction details through UX01/UX02 before P05 implementation.

items.title: Who has the strongest initial pain and buying reason?
items.context: The industrial-support IT profile is a proposed focus, not proven product-market fit.
questions: Who performs triage and patch approval, and who buys the product?
What volume, delay or repeated manual work can they demonstrate?
Which existing tools and policies constrain them?
What measurable outcome would justify adoption or payment?
items.closeWith: Recorded customer discovery with permitted evidence, competing-workflow comparison and explicit assumptions; no demand or superiority claim without evidence.
items.timing: Before committing a customer pilot or expanding scope.

items.title: Which exact releases and appliance profiles will we qualify?
items.context: Keep the narrowed Ubuntu lab path and conditional FortiOS evidence scope. Broad OT scanning or firmware execution is not implied.
questions: Which exact Ubuntu release and package fixtures can we reproduce?
Which FortiOS model/train has adequate authorized evidence, advisory semantics and supported upgrade guidance?
What stays unknown, manual or unsupported?
items.closeWith: An explicit supported-profile matrix with capability-specific fixtures and limits, reviewed against the existing qualification gates.
items.timing: Before profile-specific claims; Ubuntu qualification does not wait for FortiOS.

items.title: What real organizational data can we legally access?
items.context: Public vulnerability records are real data but do not provide a real customer inventory or policies. Synthetic scenarios stay labelled. Amr reviews advisory-source rights; Shams reviews asset-data access and collection feasibility.
questions: Can Iskraemeco or another partner provide written, scoped access to inventories, configurations or reviewed policies?
What minimization, de-identification, permissions, retention and publication restrictions apply?
What can the prototype, MVP and pilot honestly demonstrate with their available data?
items.closeWith: A data-access agreement or recorded refusal/unknown, provenance manifest and stage-specific dataset plan; proceed with public records plus declared lab/synthetic fixtures when access is absent.
items.timing: Before importing customer material or claiming real-customer evaluation.

items.title: What hardware and GPU access are actually available?
items.context: No sponsor, Iskraemeco GPU capacity or hardware commitment is assumed.
questions: What CPU/RAM/storage/GPU can the team use now, at what access limits and cost?
What concurrency, latency and model context can the measured system support?
Could partner resources be withdrawn, and what smaller-capability profile remains usable?
items.closeWith: Measured resource inventory and capacity/cost report coordinated with Hams; written access terms for any partner hardware.
items.timing: Before promising a model size, hosting capacity or training experiment.

items.title: Which deployment profile fits the first users?
items.context: On-prem is a required long-term direction. Local deployment, disconnected operation and cloud services require separate qualification.
questions: Which actual customer requirements permit public cloud, private hosting, external inference or no public egress?
Who operates updates, identity, certificates, source refreshes, backups and recovery?
What measured cost and operational burden fit the initial release and later on-prem packages?
items.closeWith: A customer-policy/deployment matrix and costed staged recommendation using the existing P14/P17 gates; no paid provider or infrastructure purchase selected here.
items.timing: Before provider purchase, pilot commitment or offline claims.

items.title: Can a data partnership support a viable commercial package?
items.context: A data revenue idea is a business hypothesis; public access or an API subscription does not establish redistribution rights. Shams retains business partnership stewardship; Amr supplies D01/D17/D18 source and rights evidence.
questions: What proprietary enrichment would a partner supply, to whom and under what contract?
Can we display, cache, redistribute, bundle or resell it in cloud and disconnected installations?
What costs, attribution, renewal, withdrawal and customer-data restrictions would apply?
Would a complete-solution package create enough customer value to cover acquisition and support costs?
items.closeWith: A BMC/value hypothesis plus rights/cost/partnership comparison; unresolved rights stay explicitly unknown and unbundled.
items.timing: Before selling or bundling third-party data.

items.title: What did “CSA Games” refer to?
items.context: Keep the original meeting phrase without guessing its meaning. Gamification and L&D remain outside the current implementation.
questions: Was this a named product, training approach, example or proposed feature?
What user problem and evidence would justify considering it later?
items.closeWith: Confirmed meaning and a deliberate future-scope or discard decision, without silently adding a workstream.
items.timing: Next discussion about this note; no current-release blocker.

items.title: What exactly are the proposed “Classic Actions”?
items.context: The existing reviewed remediation and execution path remains authoritative; this phrase adds no execution permission.
questions: Which concrete action types did the meeting intend?
Are they explanations, draft plans, evidence requests or approved mutations?
Which roles, scope, checks and recovery requirements apply to each?
items.closeWith: A small action catalogue mapped to existing contracts and permission boundaries; unknown actions remain unsupported.
items.timing: Before treating the phrase as a new product capability.

items.title: What freshness promise can we actually support?
items.context: The desired two-to-three-day window is a target to validate, not a guaranteed service level.
questions: Does the clock start at source publication, source availability, ingestion or reassessment?
How do outages, vendor delays, incomplete enrichment and disconnected bundles affect the promise?
What measurements and stale-evidence indicators must users see?
items.closeWith: A defined freshness metric with measured pipeline evidence and separately stated disconnected-snapshot limits, as required by D16.
items.timing: Before publishing an SLA or freshness claim.

items.title: How will top actions reflect organization policy?
items.context: Retain the existing grouped-action approach. Exact policy thresholds and benefit claims still need validation. Hams owns the AI-powered prioritization capability; D12 remains the cybersecurity policy baseline. Candidate selection and promotion depend on A17 comparative evidence.
questions: Which business-critical assets, exploitation signals, exposure and maintenance constraints matter?
How are missing context, incompatible actions and justified deferrals represented?
What reviewed baseline and ranking metrics demonstrate useful prioritization?
items.closeWith: A versioned reviewed policy configuration and evaluation report; show uncertainty and reasons instead of claiming a universally correct top ten.
items.timing: Before presenting a ranking as customer-qualified.

prototypeWeek.state: Internal planning targets; actual completion and available hours are unverified.
prototypeWeek.goal: By 5 November, run one authorized Ubuntu observation through a vendor-backed applicability check into a minimal read-only screen; demonstrate Hams’s evidence-retrieval component separately if model/gateway integration is not qualified.
prototypeWeek.boundary: This is Prototype Build 0.1 / a G1 slice, not the finished product, full G1 acceptance or completion of every linked package. No 10 November or 15 November final-prototype commitment is adopted. Final prototype/discussion date remains unconfirmed after midterm.
prototypeWeek.capacity: Working estimate only: 12–16 focused hours per member across 30 October–5 November, with roughly one quarter protected for review/integration inside that total. Available hours and existing code must be checked on 30 October. This is an ambitious narrow target, not a productivity claim or a promise of completion.
rhythm: Confirm existing artifacts, authorized target, one Ubuntu release, run commands and sample IDs. Freeze a usable draft contract on 30 October before building against it.
Sunday 1 November: every owner demonstrates their assigned code/output and exchanges the fixed samples; docs alone do not meet this checkpoint.
Thursday 5 November: one real host → normalized evidence → reviewed assessment → persisted API/UI result; retrieval evidence demo and honest limitations alongside it.
No new work is scheduled. Use the frozen bundle for reference; do not move missed work into exam leave.
No delivery deadlines, required meetings, reminders or prototype tasks scheduled.
Inspect what actually exists, reconfirm capacity and official discussion dates, then set the next prototype milestone. This is a planning review, not a new implementation deadline.
prototypeWeek.readinessRule: Foundation is expected to have produced reusable artifacts; the site does not establish that it is done. On 30 October, run each listed artifact once. Existing valid work is reused. A missing prerequisite becomes the first repair for that owner, not an invented DONE state.

scopeCuts: If capacity is lower than the working estimate, keep the real collection + supported assessment + read screen and reduce sample quantity/visual polish; disclose the smaller denominator.
If Friday contracts fail, repair the bounded payload first. Work on independent pure functions/fixtures; do not independently change schema names and discover divergence on Thursday.
If source access fails, preserve the error and use a dated trusted sample for coding. Mark cached/not-live; never claim D01 live-source acceptance passed.
If live collection fails, demonstrate the labelled replay path and record the real-collection gap. This is a partial checkpoint, not a successful real-host slice.
If the UI or auth slice fails, provide the read-only local/API evidence safely and record UI/auth as unfinished; do not publish an unauthenticated customer-like service.
Drop stretch work first. Do not sacrifice evidence correctness, authorization, secret handling or uncertainty display. Unfinished work stays unfinished; never silently move it into 7–12 November.
